articles.title: Sabalenka crashes out of season-ending WTA Finals after losing to Svitolina
articles.summary: World number two Sabalenka’s season came to a disappointing end after she failed to reach the WTA Finals semifinals.
articles.body:
Elina Svitolina overwhelmed Aryna Sabalenka in the deciding set to seal a ⁠6-3, 3-6, 6-1 upset on Friday and reach the semifinals of the season-ending WTA Finals in Indian Wells, where she will face Linda Noskova.

Svitolina absorbed and redirected Sabalenka’s power effectively, breaking the ⁠Belarusian six times before sealing her first victory over her opponent in more than six years with a forehand winner on her fourth match point.

With the win, Svitolina improved to 2-6 against Sabalenka in their career meetings.

“It was a bit of a roller-coaster match,” Svitolina told reporters.

“I played well in ‌the first set but lost a little bit of rhythm. She played well in the second and served much better. I was really happy with the way I could come back in the third after losing the first game.”

The Ukrainian again did not shake hands with Sabalenka after the match, maintaining her policy of not doing so with Russian and Belarusian players following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine .

Svitolina, the 2018 WTA Finals champion, will face Noskova on ⁠Saturday for a place in the final.

The defeat ended Sabalenka’s season ⁠on a disappointing note.

The second seed won Brisbane International in January and then Indian Wells and the Miami Open in March to complete the “Sunshine Double” but did not claim another title after that.

Sabalenka also surrendered the world number one ⁠ranking to Elena Rybakina at the US Open.

She had entered the season finale among the favourites after Rybakina withdrew on the eve of ⁠the tournament because of illness.

Sabalenka declined to speak to the ⁠media following Friday’s loss.

Earlier in the day, tournament debutant Andreeva continued her impressive run with a 6-2, 6-1 win over fellow Russian Diana Shnaider, her third straight-sets victory of the week.

Shnaider, Andreeva’s friend and doubles partner, replaced Karolina Muchova, who ‌withdrew before the final day of round-robin matches with a gastrointestinal illness.

Andreeva had already secured her place in the semifinals before facing Shnaider and will meet American Jessica Pegula on Saturday.

The eight-day, $10m ‌tournament was moved from Riyadh to Indian Wells Tennis Garden due to the United States-Israeli war on Iran . The event will be played in Charlotte starting next year.

articles.title: Alcaraz y su raqueta sin cordaje: "Es el tipo de trabajo que me ha hecho entender y mejorar en pista indoor"
articles.standfirst: El murciano intenta impactar la pelota en el punto dulce de la raqueta, sacando la mano hacia delante
articles.summary: El murciano intenta impactar la pelota en el punto dulce de la raqueta, sacando la mano hacia delante
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, un innovador en los entrenamientos (Mirra Andreeva confesó que le copia ejercicios en el gimnasio), empezó a trabajar con una raqueta sin cordaje en su vuelta a los entrenamientos tras la lesión en la muñeca derecha. Carlitos, totalmente recuperado ya de la dolencia que le tuvo cuatro meses y medio alejado de las pistas, explica las razones que le llevan a seguir utilizando su Babolat sin cuerdas en el inicio de sus sesiones preparatorias. "Son ejercicios para tocarla o intentar tocarla en el punto dulce de la raqueta, sacar la mano hacia delante. Es que aquí la pelota va muy rápida y tienes muy poco tiempo de margen. Si tú intentas jugar como en tierra. de tirar la pelota por arriba, al final te están comiendo. Y estos ejercicios son para intentar sacar la mano hacia delante, para tocarla siempre en el centro de la raqueta, para estar agachado, que aquí la bola no bota tanto. Es el tipo de trabajo que me ha hecho entender y mejorar en pista indoor", reflexiona el campeón de siete grandes. A Carlitos se le vio con una raqueta sin cordaje el pasado miércoles en la primera práctica realizada en el Inalpi Arena de Turín junto a su entrenador Samuel López.

articles.title: Taylor Fritz makes honest admission after winning his first indoor title in Stockholm
articles.summary: Taylor Fritz captured the first indoor title of his career after winning the Stockholm Open on Saturday. The American star, ranked 10th in the world...
articles.body:
Taylor Fritz captured the first indoor title of his career after winning the Stockholm Open on Saturday.

The American star, ranked 10th in the world currently, beat Thiago Agustin Tirante in the final of the ATP 250 event. Fritz was in cruise control in the first set, which he won 6-2, but the Argentine rallied to force a third set and took his opponent to a tiebreak.

Fritz won the shootout 7-3 to triumph 6-2, 4-6, 7-6 and claim his 12th ATP title, ending his 2026 season on a high.

Taylor Fritz reacts after winning the Stockholm Open

"It was a stressful match for sure," said Fritz in his on-court interview after the win. "I felt like I came out, I was playing really well, and then I let some opportunities slip in the second set, and then he played a good game, a really good defensive game.

"I made a couple of mistakes. He's got a big serve; he was playing well. It kind of changed the momentum of the match. I was having a really hard time breaking him after that, and it turned into a really tight war of a match."

Reacting to winning his first indoor title, Fritz said: "It feels nice. I think I've lost a lot of indoor finals, but at the same time I didn't really look too much into it because when I won Tokyo the one year, the whole tournament was pretty much played indoors, so I do kind of half feel like I've had one. But it's good to get that one; now all that's left is a clay title."

Fritz's victory comes after a disappointing end to his Paris Masters campaign, where he came close to beating eventual champion Carlos Alcaraz in the quarterfinals, but came up short. That loss also put an end to his pursuit of ATP Finals qualification.

"It's really big for me to deal with what I dealt with in Paris," said Fritz. "I wanted to go home so bad; I think anyone would. But I knew that I would feel like a quitter and be a little disappointed in myself if I did that, so I'm glad I came here and made the most of it. I'm playing great tennis, and I get to end the year with a title."

This year marked the first time in three years that Fritz has failed to qualify for the ATP Finals.

articles.title: Alcaraz y Ferrero vuelven a abrazarse en público y en privado 361 días después
articles.standfirst: Los dos no coincidían desde el 18 de noviembre de 2025 cuando se despidieron en el hotel de Bolonia
articles.summary: Los dos no coincidían desde el 18 de noviembre de 2025 cuando se despidieron en el hotel de Bolonia
articles.body: Cuando el 18 de noviembre de 2025, Carlos Alcaraz y Juan Carlos Ferrero se despidieron en el Royal Hotel Carlton de Bolonia poco podían imaginar que no volverían a abrazarse hasta este sábado en Turín, en un entrenamiento previo al inicio de las ATP Finals. Juan Carlos acompañó entonces a Carlitos a la localidad italiana, sede de la fase final de la Copa Davis. El jugador de El Palmar no pudo defender a España en la máxima competición por países a causa de un edema en el isquiotibial. Los dos estuvieron juntos en las pruebas médicas que Carlos se realizó en un hospital de la capital de la región Emilia-Romaña y cenaron después con el resto de los miembros de la selección nacional. "Va a ser un poco raro tras tanto tiempo, le voy a dar un abrazo", reconocía el murciano en su comparecencia pública del viernes tras hacerse la foto oficial junto al resto de participantes. Habían pasado 361 días desde que Alcaraz y Ferrero no cruzaban sus miradas. El primer momento se produjo al mediodía, lejos de las cámaras, según ha podido saber MARCA. Los dos se encontraron comiendo en el restaurante de 1.200 metros cuadrados que ha montado Red Bull para los tenistas y que se asemeja a los de la Fórmula Uno. El segundo abrazo se produjo en la pista central del Inalpi Arena porque Carlitos se saltó el calentamiento previo de una hora para preservar su físico tras los problemas de estómago del viernes. Apareció con una aparatosa rodillera. Juanki estaba allí junto a su nuevo pupilo, el estadounidense Ben Shelton. Se dio un tercer abrazo con Carlitos a la conclusión de la sesión preparatoria. Fue incluso más largo que los dos anteriores. Ambos trabajaron durante siete campañas y el preparador llevó al murciano a ganar seis grandes y ser el número 1 más joven de la historia. Ferrero permanecerá hasta el lunes en la capital de la región del Piamonte por lo que tendrá tiempo de ver en directo el debut de Shelton este domingo frente a Arthur Fils. Posteriormente, viajará a Asia donde tenía unos compromisos adquiridos antes de unirse profesionalmente a Shelton a finales de octubre. Su primer torneo oficial al lado del jugador estadounidense será el Open de Australia (17 al 31). Allí también estará Carlitos, que acudirá a la defensa de la corona de campeón.

articles.title: Current world No. 1 Alexander Zverev faces fresh lawsuit from ex-girlfriend over domestic abuse allegations ahead of ATP finals
articles.summary: World No. 1 Alexander Zverev is facing a civil lawsuit from former partner Brenda Patea regarding domestic abuse allegations, challenging his claims of innocence just before the ATP Finals.
articles.body: Alexander Zverev will begin his bid for a third ATP Finals title under renewed legal scrutiny after his former partner, Brenda Patea, filed a civil lawsuit over his public statements about the domestic abuse case she brought against him. The action, lodged in Berlin, challenges his claims that the allegations were disproved and that his innocence had been established, despite the earlier proceedings ending without a verdict.Brenda Patea sues Alexander Zverev over claims his innocence was provenThe lawsuit was filed on September 18, with Patea, the mother of Zverev’s five-year-old daughter, seeking legal action over comments the German tennis player made after criminal proceedings relating to her allegations were discontinued in June 2024.The case centres on Zverev’s repeated assertions that the allegations had been proven false and that his innocence had been established. Patea argues that those statements misrepresented the outcome of the proceedings and breached an agreement reached when the original case was settled.According to tennis journalist Ben Rothenberg, who first reported the new action for Bounces, Patea’s legal representatives had previously written to Zverev asking him to stop making such statements. The lawsuit says that he did not respond. Her lawyer, Michael Scheele, said the action was intended both to seek redress for his client and to prevent further statements of the same nature.“This lawsuit serves both to provide satisfaction to the plaintiff and to prevent further infringements,” Scheele said.He argued that Zverev’s comments had caused particular harm because they were made to an international publication and subsequently repeated by German media.“In the present case, a serious infringement has occurred,” Scheele said. “The defendant made a false factual assertion to an international newspaper that his innocence had been proven. This statement was disseminated internationally and picked up by numerous German media outlets.“It discredits the plaintiff as a liar and portrays her as a person who wrongfully accused the defendant. Furthermore, the defendant has breached a contractual obligation to refrain from such conduct, which makes the motive and degree of his fault particularly egregious.”The lawsuit seeks compensation for damage to Patea’s public standing, alongside an injunction intended to prevent further statements. She had initially applied for a preliminary injunction, but withdrew that application on September 14 before filing the claim four days later.The Berlin court has assigned the case a number and issued a procedural order dated November 5. However, the lawsuit had not yet been formally served on Zverev at the time of the reports. The action therefore represents a new civil dispute over his public comments, rather than a reopening of the criminal proceedings that ended in 2024.The lawsuit also sets out why Patea had previously hesitated to pursue Zverev through the courts. It says she feared reprisals from him and anticipated that he would be less willing to reach an out-of-court agreement over the child support she was seeking.Why Alexander Zverev’s original domestic abuse case ended without a verdictThe dispute stems from allegations made by Patea about an incident in Berlin in May 2020. She accused Zverev of pushing her against a wall and strangling her with both hands during an argument. Patea had made her allegations public, and Zverev has consistently denied them.On October 2, 2023, Berlin’s Tiergarten district court issued a penalty order against the tennis player, imposing a €450,000 fine. The amount was calculated through 90 daily payments of €5,000. Zverev challenged the order, preventing it from becoming final and leading to a criminal trial in 2024.Proceedings began in May that year, while Zverev was competing at the French Open, where he reached the final. The case was discontinued in June after an agreement was reached between Zverev, Patea and the prosecution.Under the settlement, Zverev agreed to pay €200,000, comprising €150,000 to the state and €50,000 to charitable organisations. Crucially, the proceedings ended without a finding of guilt or innocence, and Zverev did not admit to the allegations.The distinction became central to the statements that have now prompted Patea’s civil action. After the proceedings were discontinued, Zverev suggested during a press conference at Roland Garros that the decision itself demonstrated his innocence.“They’re not going to drop the case if you’re guilty at the end of the day. I don’t know what translations you have, but that’s what it means. Done. We move on. I never ever want to hear another question about the subject again. That goes out to everybody,” he said.He returned to the subject in a June 2025 interview with L’Équipe, conducted the morning after winning his maiden Grand Slam title at the French Open. Asked about the allegations by journalist Quentin Moynet, Zverev challenged the premise of the question.“First of all, this isn’t that kind of interview. Secondly, you know that the accusations have been proven false?” he said.When the journalist argued that the allegations remained a legitimate subject of discussion, Zverev added: “I did everything I could, and my innocence has been proven.”Patea’s new lawsuit challenges precisely that interpretation of the outcome. The criminal proceedings were discontinued following a settlement, but there was no trial verdict establishing that the allegations were false or that Zverev had been cleared.Zverev faces renewed scrutiny as he prepares for ATP FinalsThe lawsuit arrives at a significant moment in Zverev’s career. The German has risen to world No. 1 and secured the year-end top ranking for 2026, and is preparing to compete at the ATP Finals in Turin, where the tournament begins on Sunday. He will be seeking a third title at the season-ending championship.The new legal action is not the first time Zverev has faced allegations of abuse involving a former partner. Olya Sharypova, another former girlfriend and a former tennis player, made allegations against him in October 2020, describing incidents of alleged physical and emotional abuse during their relationship in 2019. She said some of the incidents occurred in cities where ATP tournaments were being held.Zverev denied Sharypova’s allegations. The ATP opened an investigation that lasted 15 months before announcing in January 2023 that it would take no disciplinary action, citing insufficient evidence to substantiate the claims.That investigation was separate from the criminal proceedings brought by Patea in Germany. The ATP’s decision concerned whether there was sufficient evidence for disciplinary action under its own rules; the Berlin case involved allegations examined through the German criminal justice system.Zverev has denied the allegations made by both women. The new lawsuit does not establish liability, and its claims will have to be considered through the civil proceedings. It does, however, bring his public account of the Patea case back into focus just as he prepares for one of the biggest tournaments of his season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: WTA Finals: Mirra Andreeva eliminates Jessica Pegula to reach final, winning in straight sets after 'diva' criticism
articles.summary: Mirra Andreeva beat Jessica Pegula in straight sets in their semi-final to reach the title match at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells; They were playing each other after Pegula was overheard calling Andreeva a "diva" earlier in the tournament; Andreeva had the last word, winning 6-3 6-4
articles.body:
Andreeva's 6-3 6-4 victory saw her advance to the final at the year-end tournament in California, making her the first teenager to reach the title match at the WTA Finals since 2004.

Andreeva and Pegula were playing one another for the first time in their careers and their match-up in the last four came after Pegula had been picked up on a hot mic criticising Andreeva at the start of the tournament.

In a livestreamed practice session, Pegula was heard labelling Andreeva a "diva" who "needs to be humbled".

Andreeva had the last word as she eliminated the American from the tournament. To win Andreeva had to come back from being a break down in both sets.

Pegula broke first in the opening set but Andreeva immediately responded to force a break back her way.

Andreeva smashed a forehand cross-court to claim another break and leave her serving for the set.

She managed to see it out, but only after Pegula squandered a break point.

In the second set another break of serve saw Andreeva move 5-3 up and enjoy control of the contest. Pegula did hold serve after that but Andreeva closed out the contest in her next service game.

"It was a tough match," Andreeva said. "You have to work hard to win ​a point against her. She is going to leave everything out there and make your life complicated, so I ​wanted to make her life complicated as ⁠well today."

Andreeva, appearing in the WTA Finals for the first time, has not dropped a set in four matches at the event so far.

Ukraine's Elina Svitolina will meet Andreeva in the final after she dismantled the reigning Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova.

Svitolina won 6-2 6-1, winning rapidly and almost shutting Noskova entirely out of the second set.

The Andreeva-Svitolina final will be a rematch after the two played each other earlier in this competition format. Since losing to the Russian in the group stage of these WTA Finals, Svitolina has staged an extraordinary resurgence and was in outstanding form by the time she met Noskova in their semi-final.

articles.title: WTA Finals results: Elina Svitolina beats Linda Noskova and Mirra Andreeva sees off Jessica Pegula
articles.summary: Elina Svitolina drops just three games as she thrashes Linda Noskova to set up a WTA Finals showpiece against Mirra Andreeva.
articles.body:
Elina Svitolina dropped just three games as she thrashed Linda Noskova to set up a WTA Finals showpiece against Mirra Andreeva.

Ukraine's Svitolina was composed and aggressive in a 6-2 6-1 victory over Wimbledon champion Noskova in just 64 minutes.

It caps a remarkable turnaround for world number six Svitolina in Indian Wells, having suffered a heavy defeat in her opening group match against Andreeva.

However, she has shown all of her fighting spirit to win her next three matches, including snapping a six-match losing streak to Aryna Sabalenka on Friday.

Svitolina now has 11 wins over top-10 opponents this year - the most of any player on the WTA Tour.

"After losing the first match I was ready to go home, and now I'm in the final," the 32-year-old said.

"I will do my homework with my coaches - I will try to win a bit more games than I did in the first match [against Andreeva]."

Svitolina is back in the world's top 10 for the first time since October 2021.

She took maternity leave in May 2022 to have daughter Skai, and has made an effort to play more aggressive tennis since her return.

She returned brilliantly against Noskova, neutralising the Czech's big serve from the first game.

Noskova was well below her best, hitting 11 double faults and committing 27 unforced errors to Svitolina's 18.

It is the third time Svitolina has reached the final of the season-ending tournament, having lifted the trophy in 2018.

Earlier, Andreeva became the youngest player for 22 years to reach the WTA Finals showpiece with a composed victory over Jessica Pegula.

French Open champion Andreeva came back from a break down in both sets to win 6-3 6-4.

The 19-year-old Russian is the youngest finalist at the season-ending event since Maria Sharapova, who was 17 when she won the title in 2004.

Victory over American Pegula ensures Andreeva will finish the year as world number two.

"I did not feel one bit of pressure today, I don't know why," Andreeva told Sky Sports.

"Usually I feel like on these important points or when I have to close out the match or the set I get so tight.

"But for some reason today I was just playing. I was just not thinking about anything, just trying to enjoy."

Tournament debutant Andreeva has yet to drop a set and has not lost more than four games in any of her eight sets.

The 18 games she has lost is the fewest for a finalist at the WTA Finals since the round-robin format was introduced in 2003.

Under the guidance of coach Conchita Martinez, Andreeva has developed her serve into a real weapon.

She won 77% of points behind her first serve and hit 17 winners to outmuscle Pegula.

Andreeva also showed impressive composure, remaining unfazed despite going an early break down in both sets against the home favourite.

articles.title: WTA Finals: Aryna Sabalenka apologises after viral clip of her swearing during Elina Svitolina defeat
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka apologises and denies claims she insulted opponent Elina Svitolina after a viral clip showed her swearing during her WTA Finals defeat by the Ukrainian.
articles.body:
Aryna Sabalenka has apologised and denied claims that she insulted opponent Elina Svitolina after a viral clip showed her swearing during her WTA Finals defeat by the Ukrainian.

A video of world number two Sabalenka angrily gesturing and swearing in Russian during her 6-3 3-6 6-1 defeat by Ukraine's Svitolina was posted on social media on Saturday.

Some commentators interpreted Belarusian Sabalenka's comments as an insult towards Svitolina or Ukrainians in general.

Sabalenka later wrote on social media that "my comment was not directed at Elina" but she lost her temper because of the behaviour of some fans.

"I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment," the 28-year-old wrote.

"That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone offended."

Sabalenka said Svitolina had played a great match, adding that she wished her "all the best for the rest of the tournament".

Ukrainian players have a long-standing policy of not shaking hands with Russian or Belarusian players because of the ongoing invasion of their country.

They also do not take pre-match photographs with each other.

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka Apologizes After Viral Video of Comments Toward Fans During Loss to Elina Svitolina
articles.summary: Belarusian tennis star Aryna Sabalenka issued an apology after her on-court outburst went viral following her WTA Finals loss to Ukraine's Elina Svitolina.
articles.body:
Belarusian tennis star Aryna Sabalenka issued an apology after her on-court outburst went viral following her WTA Finals loss to Ukraine's Elina Svitolina.

"I want to clarify something from my recent match that has been circulating online," Sabalenka wrote in a Saturday Instagram story . "My comment was not directed at Elina. I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment.

"That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologize to anyone I offended."

Sabalenka tied Friday night's group stage match in the second set before Svitolina closed out with a dominant deciding set to advance to the WTA Finals semifinals with a 6-3, 3-6, 6-1 victory at Indian Wells.

The win allowed Svitolina to advance to play Linda Nosková in Saturday's semifinals while snapping a five-match losing streak to Sabalenka that dated back to the quarterfinals of the 2023 French open.

The two competitors did not shake hands after the match. Svitolina, like other Ukrainian tennis players, has declined since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine to shake the hands of Russian or Belarusian competitors.

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka clarifies profane WTA Finals comment was about Ukrainian fans in stands, not opponent Elina Svitolina
articles.summary: The former WTA No. 1 also fell to No. 3 in the rankings on Saturday
articles.body:
It's probably safe to say the WTA Finals did not go as planned for Aryna Sabalenka.

The former WTA No. 1 entered the year-end tournament looking to bounce back after losing that top ranking to Elena Rybakina . Instead, she dropped from No. 2 to No. 3 in the rankings and found herself clarifying an ugly on-court moment via social media on Saturday.

That moment came during Sabalenka's final round-robin match against Elina Svitolina, which the Ukrainian veteran won 6-3, 3-6, 6-1 to reach the semifinals and eliminate Sabalenka.

During the third set, one X account noticed Sabalenka appeared to be complaining in Russian about, well, something involving Ukraine . Via lip-reading, the post speculated Sabalenka was either saying "Those f***ing Ukrainians, for f***'s sake!" or "That f***ing Ukrainian b****, for f***'s sake!"?

The clip soon went viral, to the point that Sabalenka felt the need to respond via her Instagram story . The Belarusian star did not specify what exactly she said, only that it was directed at a group of fans cheering against her rather than for Svitolina.

Regardless, Sabalenka apologized. The full statement:

I want to clarify something from my recent match that has been circulating online. My comment was not directed at Elina. I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment. That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and l apologise to anyone l offended. Elina played a great match, and I wish her all the best for the rest of the tournament.

It's been an emotionally raw situation around Svitolina in particular after announcing her divorce from beloved French player Gael Monfils last month .

Less than two hours after Sabalenka posted her statement, Svitolina finished off a 6-2, 6-1 win over 2026 Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova to reach her first final at the tournament since 2019. That match will be against the French Open champion Mirra Andreeva in another Russia-Ukraine match.

It was Andreeva who leapfrogged Sabalenka for No. 2 in the WTA live rankings by reaching the final on Saturday. In her round-robin match against Sabalenka, the 19-year-old fell behind 4-1 in the first set then won 11 straight games, and 45 of the last 55 points, for an impressive victory.

Andreeva has now won eight straight sets at the WTA Finals, including a 6-3, 6-4 win over Jessica Pegula in the semifinals on Saturday. As for Sabalenka, she is now 2-4 since losing the US Open final to Rybakina, including a first-round upset against Ann Li at the Wuhan Open.

articles.standfirst: Sólo el número 1 mundial, su rival este domingo, ha jugado y ha ganado más que el madrleño
articles.summary: Sólo el número 1 mundial, su rival este domingo, ha jugado y ha ganado más que el madrleño
articles.body: Rafa Jódar, a sus 20 años, muestra la tranquilidad del que ha hecho bien su trabajo al mismo tiempo de querer más. El madrileño es el tenista que más rápido se ha colado en el top10 desde su primer torneo como profesional -actualmente es el noveno del ranking- y el primero en jugar las ATP Finals en su estreno en el circuito. Él no ha pagado la novatada. A estas alturas, la pasada campaña, era el 167 del mundo y estaba esperando su participación en las Next Gen Finals de Jeddah, donde quedó eliminado en la fase de grupos. Jódar se clasificó para la cita de maestros de Turín con una triple carambola, en la que Alex de Miñaur perdió en la segunda ronda de París, y Tommy Paul y Taylor Fritz se quedaron en cuartos. Este último disfrutó de dos pelotas de victoria frente a Carlos Alcaraz. Rafa y su padre, que responde al mismo nombre, sufrieron por separado viendo el partido en Madrid. El octavo y último billete del joven de Leganés era un premio a la regularidad. Suma 78 duelos jugados, de los que ganó 58. Podrían ser 86 si alcanza la final en Turín y en la Copa Davis: “Ha sido un año donde las cosas han ido muy rápido, pero jugando tanto no te da tiempo a asimilarlo. Me tomo este torneo y la Davis como un premio. Físicamente vengo bien. He jugado mucho, pero es gracias a los resultados”, reflexiona. Sólo Alexander Zverev jugó y ganó más que él entre la élite. Sascha será su rival hoy en la apertura oficial del torneo. Zverev dispara sus cifras hasta los 83 partidos jugados, de los que 65 cayeron a su favor. El jugador de Hamburgo se ha hecho merecedor del número 1 a final de curso, cuyo trofeo le será entregado mañana. “Aquí están los mejores del mundo. De pequeño siempre sueñas con jugar con ellos en este tipo de torneos”, sentencia Rafa.

articles.body: Las finales de la WTA de Indian Wells van a tener un sorprendente desenlace. La final la protagonizarán Mirra Andreeva y Elina Svitolina, con una bolsa en premios de algo más de tres millones de dólares. Se repite el partido de la primera ronda del 'round robin'. A la ucraniana poco o nada le ha importado ser señalada en las últimas fechas como la culpable del hundimiento anímico de su exmarido, el también tenista, Gael Monfils, tras su separación. Monfils, que ha colgado la raqueta en 2026, declinó las invitaciones de Lyon y París para despedirse del tenis jugando. Posteriormente, la federación francesa de tenis le ha nombrado como nuevo capitán de la Copa Davis. Svitolina, verdugo de Aryna Sabalenka, derrotó en las semifinales a Linda Noskova, campeona de Wimbledon, por un contundente 6-2 y 6-1. Se vio de todo menos igualdad en la centrak del Tennis Garden. Antes, Andreeva había silenciado con tenis a Jessica Pegula, por 6-3 y 6-4. La estadounidense, en la previa del torneo, la había acusado de ser "una diva" y había culpado de ello a su entrenadora, la aragonesa Conchita Martínez. Mirra, de 19 años, se ha asegurado terminar el curso en el segundo puesto del ranking WTA, sólo por detrás de Rybakina y por delante de la irregular Sabalenka. Svitolina podría acabar cuarta en caso de coronarse maestra del tenis femenino.

articles.title: “Even More Dangerous” – Toni Nadal Warns About Alcaraz & Sinner’s “Trouble” After Ben Shelton & Juan Carlos Ferrero Team Up At ATP Finals
articles.summary: Toni Nadal believes that Ben Shelton, under the tutelage of Juan Carlos Ferrero, will be a much bigger threat to Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner, and Alexander...
articles.body:
Toni Nadal believes that Ben Shelton, under the tutelage of Juan Carlos Ferrero, will be a much bigger threat to Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner, and Alexander Zverev in 2027 than he has been so far. Shelton and Ferrero's partnership is officially set to begin in the offseason. However, Ferrero has already overseen one of the Americans' practice sessions at the ATP Finals in Turin.

Ferrero is in Turin for the ATP No. 1 Club gala, and he made the most of the opportunity to meet Shelton. The former World No. 1 Spaniard was spotted guiding the American as he practiced ahead of the men's year-end championships. Bryan, Shelton's father, will continue as his son's primary coach, with Ferrero set to play a largely complementary role in the American's coaching setup.

Speaking to Spanish outlet Sport , Nadal touched on Shelton being coached by Ferrero, who previously coached Alcaraz, and had plenty of positive things to say about the exciting new partnership. The iconic coach, who spearheaded his nephew Rafael's charge to the very top of men's tennis, had this to say: (quotes translated from Spanish via Google)

"Obviously, for Shelton it is a very good choice to have Juan Carlos Ferrero. In addition to being a great player, he has been with Carlos for a long time and knows where to do him a little damage. I also think that, because of his mentality, he can be of great help to the American."

"Shelton has great potential: a great serve, a good mentality and forehand. His game lacks a little order, and I think that is, above all, what Juan Carlos is going to contribute. So he will be an even more dangerous rival next year. He is a young player who can put Carlos, Sinner and Zverev in trouble. So we will have an interesting tennis season."

Shelton broke new ground in 2026, reaching his first Major final at the US Open after beating Alcaraz in the quarterfinals. However, he could not get past Zverev at the last hurdle.

More recently, at the Paris Masters, Alcaraz beat him in straight sets in the final. Overall, the American has losing head-to-head records against Zverev, Sinner and Alcaraz—a clear indication that he has yet to reach the standards set by the current ATP top 3.

Ben Shelton to get ATP Finals 2026 campaign underway with Round Robin phase clash against tournament debutant Arthur Fils

Arthur Fils of France, making his ATP Finals debut this year, is Ben Shelton's first Round Robin phase opponent in Turin. Fils and Shelton's head-to-head is 2-1 in the American's favor ahead of what should be an intriguing match. Zverev and young Rafael Jodar of Spain are also in the same group as Fils and Shelton. The other group consists of Alcaraz, Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli and Frances Tiafoe.

Zverev and Medvedev are the two players at the 2026 ATP Finals who have won the year-end championships before. However, this time around, Alcaraz is the favorite on paper to go all the way and win his maiden ATP Finals title.

Since returning from injury at the US Open, the Spaniard has been in rampant form, picking up titles in Tokyo, Vienna and Paris before arriving in Turin.

articles.title: WTA Finals: Aryna Sabalenka apologises for on-court outburst after defeat to Elina Svitolina
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka was knocked out of the WTA Finals by Elina Svitolina after she suffered a 6-3 3-6 6-1 defeat to the Ukrainian on Friday; Svitolina will take on Mirra Andreeva in Sunday's final, watch the match live on Sky Sports Tennis from 8pm
articles.body:
Video circulating widely on social media appeared to show Sabalenka swearing in a tirade during Friday's 6-3 3-6 6-1 loss at the season-ending championships in Indian Wells.

The former top-ranked player from Belarus said on Saturday she was upset by the behaviour of spectators during the match.

"My comment was not directed at Elina," Sabalenka posted on Instagram, without mentioning what she said.

"I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment.

"That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone I offended. Elina played a great match, and I wish her all the best for the rest of the tournament."

Svitolina did not shake hands with Sabalenka following the match.

The Ukrainian has maintained a stance of refusing to shake hands with Russian and Belarusian players following Russia's invasion of her country in 2022.

Ukrainian players also do not take pre-match photographs with Russian and Belarusian players.

She was booed at the French Open in 2023, when she refused to shake Russian-born player Anna Blinkova's hand.

In the quarter-finals of the same event, Svitolina was beaten 6-4 6-4 by Sabalenka, and was again booed after she refused to shake the world No 2's hand.

Sabalenka previously said that she "respected" Svitolina's decision not to shake hands with Russian and Belarusian players and "didn't deserve" to be booed.

Svitolina is now set to play Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva in Sunday's final of the $10 million event, live on Sky Sports.

Sabalenka was visibly annoyed during the match, and she declined to speak with media afterwards.

"There's many flags and many Ukrainian supporters are here and of course they want me to win in this particular match," Svitolina said when asked about Sabalenka's online post.

"I have seen a glimpse of it because obviously it's on social media, but yeah, I just hope the matches between us are respected. Sometimes in some matches there are not great comments towards me in regard to the war.

"It is like this on social media sometimes that things are turned around a little bit," she said.

Reflecting on Sabalenka's comments, Svitolina called for fans to show more respect to both players.

"I think we played many times, with Aryna. She has her fans, I have my fans," she told reporters, following her 6-2 6-1 win against Linda Noskova on Saturday.

"Every country, every match that we've played has been kind of different.

"I have seen a glimpse of it [the video] because obviously it's on social media."

articles.title: Jódar cede ante la jerarquía de Zverev en su debut en las ATP Finals
articles.standfirst: El número 1, campeón en las ediciones de 2018 y 2021, ejerce como tal en la apertura del torneo
articles.summary: El número 1, campeón en las ediciones de 2018 y 2021, ejerce como tal en la apertura del torneo
articles.body: Más que pagar la novatada, Rafa Jódar ha cedido este domingo su primer partido en unas ATP Finals porque sencillamente el rival es mejor. Alexander Zverev, número 1 mundial por méritos propios, no en vano ha ganado dos títulos de Grand Slam este curso, en Roland Garros y US Open, ha acabado con la resistencia del joven madrileño, por 6-4 y 6-4. Sascha, en su novena presencia en la fiesta reservada a los ocho mejores (8-1 en su primer partido del 'round robin'), dominó de principio a fin con sus enormes palancas, que le facilita el hecho de ser el más alto de todos los participantes, con su 1,98 metros, la mista estatura de Daniil Medvedev. Su jerarquía se nota también en su equipación. La marca de raquetas Head le ha personalizada una bolsa dorada por ser el mejor tenista del momento y Adidas le ha fabricado una chaqueta de vestir con el número 1 en el dorso y los trofeos de París y Nueva York en las mangas. Antes del partido se había hecho un homenaje a una representación de los mejores de la historia. Zverev no estuvo en la foto porque estaba concentrado para la batalla. Sí estaba en la instantánea el ídolo local Jannik Sinner, baja en el torneo por su lesión en la rodilla. Le secundaban Ilie Nastase, Mats Wilander, Stefan Edberg, Thomas Muster, Boris Becker, Yevgeny Kafelnikov, Marat Safin, Gustavo Kuerten, Lleyton Hewitt y Juan Carlos Ferrero. Jódar, como siempre, no regaló un solo punto. Luchó y luchó. Salvó las dos primeras pelotas de rotura en el quinto juego. No pudo con las del séptimo. En pista estaban los dos jugadores que más victorias acumulan en 2026 entre la élite: 65 a 58. El de Leganés, con la ayuda de su padre Rafa desde la banda, tuvo la opción de reengancharse al primer set, con un 5-4 y 15-40. Entonces llegaron dos misiles del alemán, con puntas de 225 kilómetros por hora. Restar eso en una superficie tan rápida como la del Inalpi Arena es una misión casi imposible. Zverev puso una marcha más al inicio del segundo acto, que le valió para lograr otro tempranero break. El jugador alemán tiene un guante en el revés y Rafa iba al límite en los intercambios. Sascha recibirá este lunes el trofeo que le acredita como el primero del ranking a final de curso. Merecido lo tiene. Ya es líder del grupo John McEnroe y el martes espera al ganador del partido que disputarán esta noche Ben Shelton y Arthur Fils. Rafa jugará con el que pierda. En la cita de maestros todo cuenta. A pesar de la derrota en dos sets, los ocho juegos sumados por Jódar pueden tener su peso en oro en caso de doble o triple empate al final de la fase de grupos. El tenista del Chamartín se ha asegurado terminar la temporada en el 'top10'. Ahora mismo es décimo después de verse superado por Taylor Fritz, campeón en Estocolmo.

articles.title: ATP Finals: Alexander Zverev beats Rafael Jodar for first win as world number one
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev claims his first victory as world number one as he sweeps aside Rafael Jodar in the opening match of the ATP Finals.
articles.body:
Alexander Zverev claimed his first victory as world number one as he swept aside Rafael Jodar in the opening match of the ATP Finals.

Germany's Zverev produced a serving masterclass to beat the fast-rising Spaniard 6-4 6-4.

The French and US Open champion dropped only 10 points on serve, landing an astonishing 84% of first serves and hitting 10 aces.

The only time Zverev looked troubled was when he went two break points down as he served for the opening set - before saving them with back-to-back aces.

"I still think I have a lot of things to improve. It was not a perfect match but to start the tournament, I am very happy," the 29-year-old said.

"Winning always helps, but it's been a good match."

Zverev lost his first match as world number one at the Paris Masters in November and said afterwards he was "annoyed" at the reaction to his rise to the top of the rankings.

He has taken full advantage of a year in which Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner have struggled with injuries, winning two majors and reaching the Wimbledon final.

Zverev underlined his status as the world's best player by walking out on court in Turin in a custom black leather jacket with a number one printed on the back and carrying a gold racquet bag.

His performance was just as befitting of his position as he put constant pressure on the Jodar serve and dominated with his own first strike.

The 20-year-old Jodar is one of the brightest talents in the men's game, having started the year outside the world's top 150.

Now ranked 11th, he fought hard to stay in touch with Zverev, but could find no way through his serve.

Zverev broke him early in the first set with a fine backhand down the line and went up a quick break in the second.

He had three further chances for a double-break lead but Jodar saved them, before Zverev served out victory.

In the doubles, Britain's Henry Patten and Finnish partner Harri Heliovaara began their campaign with a 6-3 5-7 10-4 win over Brazilian pair Rafael Matos and Orlando Luz.

Wimbledon champions Patten and Heliovaara are the defending champions in Turin.

articles.title: Sabalenka se disculpa por sus insultos a unos aficionados ucranianos en su partido ante Svitolina
articles.standfirst: La bielorrusa, eliminada a manos de la ucraniana, insultó a un grupo de espectadores de la grada tras un punto en el tercer set
articles.summary: La bielorrusa, eliminada a manos de la ucraniana, insultó a un grupo de espectadores de la grada tras un punto en el tercer set
articles.body: Aryna Sabalenka no ha tenido su mejor temporada. Levantó el 'Sunshine Double' (doblete de Indian Wells y Miami Open) en marzo, pero desde ese momento, no ha sabido cosechar grandes éxitos como líder del ranking WTA. Una condición que perdió a manos de Rybakina en la última edición del US Open. Esta semana, fue eliminada de las WTA Finals de Indian Wells ante Elina Svitolina. En el cuarto juego del tercer set, la bielorrusa se dirigió de forma despectiva a unos aficionados ucranianos que había en la grada, y un día después, ha decidido disculparse en sus redes sociales. Sabalenka publicó una historia en su cuenta de Instagram asegurando que las palabras no iban hacia su rival, pidiendo disculpas por una posible ofensa al público ucraniano: "Quiero aclarar algo sobre mi último partido que ha estado circulando online. Mi comentario no iba dirigido a Elina. Estaba frustrada con un pequeño grupo de espectadores que celebraban mis errores de forma agresiva, y reaccioné de manera impulsiva en ese momento", comenzaba el comunicado Aryna. "Dicho esto, debería haber gestionado mi frustración de otra manera, y pido disculpas a cualquier persona a la que haya podido ofender. Elina jugó un gran partido y le deseo todo lo mejor para el resto del torneo", concluyó la campeona de cuatro grandes. De las últimas 97 semanas, Sabalenka ha sido líder del ranking WTA en 88 de ellas. Algo que no ha podido demostrar con grandes títulos. Siempre ha sufrido un colapso en algún momento de los cuatro Grand Slam de la temporada: Cedió en la final del Australian Open ante Rybakina; fue sorprendida por Diana Shnaider en los cuartos de Roland Garros; se despidió de manera repentina en los octavos de Wimbledon ante Naomi Osaka; y volvió a ceder en la final del US Open ante Rybakina. Un índice de 48 victorias y 13 derrotas, tres títulos, y casi todo el año como líder del circuito, pero eso le sabe a poco a la bielorrusa, que ahora ve a la kazaja Rybakina ser la primera en el ranking. Y para colmo, Mirra Andreeva también la relevará como segunda raqueta mundial.

articles.title: ATP Finals: World No 1 Alexander Zverev begins campaign with convincing straight-sets victory over Rafael Jodar
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev beat Spain's Rafael Jodar 6-4 6-4 as the ATP Finals begins in Turin; Jodar is the first man to qualify for the Finals in the same season as his tour-level debut; You can watch the Nitto ATP Finals from November 15-22 in Turin on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
Zverev claimed his first two Grand Slam titles this year and became world No 1 for the first time too.

He is aiming for his third ATP Finals trophy after taking the season-ending event in 2018 and 2021.

"It's been a very good year for me. A lot of things that I've wanted to achieve I have achieved this year," Zverev said. "But playing here you can never take it for granted."

The 20-year-old Jodar is the first man to qualify for the Finals in the same season as his tour-level debut.

The 6ft 6ins Zverev dominated with his serve, cranking out 10 aces on the fast indoor surface, and consistently applied pressure on Jodar's serve.

It was a convincing performance for Zverev after entering on a two-match losing streak that included a straight-set loss to Lorenzo Musetti in his first match as world No 1.

The only time Zverev got in trouble was when he faced two break points while attempting to serve out the first set. He hit an ace on the first break point and a service winner on the second, then landed another ace before closing the set out.

"To start the tournament with a 6-4, 6-4 win is always very, very nice," Zverev said.

"I still think I have a lot of things to improve. It was not a perfect match."

articles.title: What Ben Shelton has already been spotted working on in training with Juan Carlos Ferrero at the ATP Finals
articles.summary: Ben Shelton is among the early starters at the ATP Finals, where he has been joined by his new coach Juan Carlos Ferrero. Shelton plays...
articles.body:
Ben Shelton is among the early starters at the ATP Finals, where he has been joined by his new coach Juan Carlos Ferrero.

Shelton plays against Arthur Fils on day one of the year-end tournament in Turin, after top seed Alexander Zverev meets Rafael Jodar. The quartet have been drawn in the John McEnroe Group of the ATP Finals , with the Ivan Lendl Group comprising Carlos Alcaraz, Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli and Frances Tiafoe.

Shelton is the third seed in Turin, where the ATP superstar and Ferrero have been working hard in practice in order to get off to the best possible start. And according to Brad Gilbert , they have already been working on a key area.

What Ben Shelton is already working on with Juan Carlos Ferrero

Speaking on The Big T Podcast from the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, Gilbert said: "I saw JCF on the court with Ben Shelton, and already it looked like they were taking time on the forehand, the forehand swing, and definitely kind of making his presence felt in practice.

"I'm glad that he came there because last year Ben did not play well. He went 0 and three, and so making his presence felt. And it was interesting that he had obviously not seen the whole Carlos Alcaraz team which he had put together, and Carlos, in 11 months, looked like he had nice hugs for everybody there."

Alcaraz won six Grand Slam titles under the guidance of Ferrero, but the Spaniards have now gone from teammates to rivals. However, the pair clearly have no hard feelings despite their split, having shared a very warm embrace during ATP Finals practice.

Brad Gilbert surprised by Ben Shelton hiring Juan Carlos Ferrero

Ferrero teased his new student for some time before eventually confirming his partnership with Shelton, which surprised many. Gilbert, who previously coached WTA star Coco Gauff, was certainly in that camp.

"You kind of feel like too that this thing came together very quickly," he said. "I think it was a great decision. No one saw this coming. Everyone thought for sure, maybe he would go with one of the young players. Jodar, maybe it would be a [Joao] Fonseca, I kind of thought maybe a [Jakub] Mensik.

"I probably didn't even think of Ben because of such a tight bond with his dad. And there are a lot of father-son coaching relationships now on the men's tour, even in the top 25 in the rankings. So this one will be very interesting to see where it goes.

"And I like the fact that they are starting here, which I think will help them learn each other a little more for the off-season. Because I do think the off-season, even though it's short, is still such an important time to make changes in your game. You don't get a lot of time, but I think that's an important time if you are really going to make some changes in your game."

And suggesting that Shelton can improve on his 0-3 record on debut at the 2025 ATP Finals, Gilbert added: "You figure with his serve indoors… I mean, 0-3 okay in his first time, but you would hope and think that the second time, as good of a year as he's had, that he can make a semi. Obviously it would be better to do better, but you certainly don't want to have another clunker.

"Because I do think if you go -3, which we saw happen here [at the WTA Finals], it is a bit of a clunker going into the off-season. Look at somebody like a Marta Kostyuk, who had such a great year, but finished the year, believe it or not, on a seven-match losing streak.

"So even though you had the best year of your career, it kind of takes it into a tough off-season. Do I need some time away? How quickly do you want to get to work? So that's why I think it is really important every match there you don't phone in anything."

An alternate in Indian Wells, Kostyuk lost all three of her WTA Finals matches , which is an unwanted record that Shelton suffered in the men's tournament this time last year. He was beaten by Zverev, Felix Auger-Aliassime and Jannik Sinner.

articles.body: Mirra Andreeva, novata, es la maestra de la WTA en 2026 tras derrotar a Elina Svitolina, por 7-5 y 6-3, en 1 hora y 48 minutos. La rusa, tildada de "diva" por parte de Jessica Pegula en la previa del torneo, ha sido la mejor en el certamen de las ocho mejores celebrado en las pistas del Tennis Garden de Indian Wells. Ha ganado sus cinco partidos sin ceder un solo set. No hubo saludo entre la joven rusa y la veterana tenista ucraniana. Mirra sí nombro a la otra finalista en la ceremonia de premiación. La presencia española fue la de Garbiñe Muguruza, directora de la competición. La flamante vencedorra es la tercera jugadora en la historia del evento en ganar en su debut sin perder mangas, después de Chris Evert en 1972 y Serena Williams en 2001. Andreeva, a sus 19 años, es la vigésimo octava tenista coronada en el Masters femenino. La pupila de Conchita Martínez toma el relevo en el palmarés de Elena Rybakina, baja de última hora. La moscovita se afianza como número 2 mundial, inmediatamente por detrás de la kazaja, a tan sólo 293 puntos de tocar la cima. Mirra se lleva un talón de algo más de tres millones de dólares y un Mercedes, espónsor principal del circuito femenino. Tendrá que sacarse el carnet de conducir si quiere conducirlo. La tenista residente en Cannes finaliza por todo lo alto una temporada en la que ganó su primer título de Grand Slam en la tierra de Roland Garros. Para encontrar a la última rusa campeona del Masters femenino hay que remontarse a Maria Sharapova, en 2004. La victoria de Andreeva es la quinta frente a una 'top10' en la campaña que ahora termina. Sus 55 victorias la convierten en la más joven en liderar el ranking de partidos ganados en una temporada desde Caroline Wozniacki, en 2009.

articles.title: Andreeva defeats Svitolina to win WTA Finals
articles.summary: Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva battled past Elina Svitolina in straight sets to win the season-ending WTA Finals crown on Sunday.She is only the third teena...
articles.body:
Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva battled past Elina Svitolina in straight sets to win the season-ending WTA Finals crown on Sunday.

Andreeva powered to a 7-5, 6-3 victory in a hard-fought duel in Indian Wells to complete a superb week in California.

Reigning French Open champion Andreeva, 19, clinched the title without dropping a set in the tournament.

She is only the third teenager after Chris Evert and Maria Sharapova to win the WTA Finals on their debut.

"It feels amazing, of course I'm super-privileged to put my name in that group," said Andreeva.

The teenager thanked friends, family and support staff in a victory speech, before light-heartedly thanking herself for her success.

"I want to thank myself for always doing the hard work, for never quitting, for always believing in myself, for not taking the days off, for working every day, and for committing to what I have to do," said Andreeva, wearing a track-suit top with the slogan "I want to thank myself."

A grueling 1hr 48min duel saw Andreeva secure a break in the opening game of the first set before holding for a 2-0 lead.

Ukrainian veteran Svitolina broke back in the fourth game, conjuring a sublime angled volley to level at 2-2.

Svitolina was soon back under pressure though, conceding another break to go 4-3 down before Andreeva held for a 5-3 lead.

There was more drama to follow when Andreeva served for the first set at 5-4 up.

She opened with back-to-back double faults to go 0-30 down, and then yanked a wild forehand wide to give Svitolina two break points at 15-40.

A long forehand gave Svitolina the break to knot it at 5-5 but Andreeva hit back immediately with her third break of serve to regain the advantage at 6-5.

The Russian made no mistake when serving for the set for a second time, holding comfortably to go 1-0 up.

The second set followed a familiar pattern, with both players trading some brutal groundstrokes in a series of long rallies.

Andreeva broke to take the lead at 1-0 but Svitolina responded in a marathon second game, breaking back after converting her seventh break point to level at 1-1.

Andreeva edged back in front with a break to go 3-2 up and then held for a 4-2 lead.

The next two games went with serve to leave Svitolina serving to stay in the match at 5-3 down.

A fortunate net cord left Andreeva with three match points at 0-40.

Svitolina saved the first and looked poised to save another, only to hit a wide open overhead smash into the net to give Andreeva the win.

Svitolina, who had been thumped 6-4, 6-0 by Andreeva in the opening round-robin game of the tournament, took positives from her performance.

"After the first match I was not expecting to play in the final," Svitolina said. "Unfortunately it didn't go my way but I gave it my all."

articles.title: Mirra Andreeva has message for Elina Svitolina in winner’s speech immediately after beating her at the WTA Finals
articles.summary: Mirra Andreeva has sent a heartfelt message of commiserations to Elina Svitolina after beating her in the final of the WTA Finals. After one hour...
articles.body:
Mirra Andreeva has sent a heartfelt message of commiserations to Elina Svitolina after beating her in the final of the WTA Finals.

After one hour and 48 minutes in Indian Wells, Andreeva defeated Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 to secure the title. The Russian superstar has emerged victorious on her WTA Finals debut. But rather than focus on her own stunning success, Andreeva was quick to praise Svitolina after their exciting encounter.

Mirra Andreeva congratulates Elina Svitolina after WTA Finals final

In a classy winner's speech, the 19-year-old said to her opponent: "I just want to congratulate Elina and the team for an amazing week. You had an amazing season, I know it's tough to lose in the final but you had such an amazing season.

"You have a young daughter, you are an amazing Mom to come back and do this. It's super hard. I would not know how hard it is to come back and do that so congratulations for that and to your team as well. I wish you the best of luck for next season."

She added: "It feels amazing to be part of this amazing group of people. Of course I am super privileged to have put my name in that group. I am super grateful for my team for pushing me every day for working to my limits and pushing me some days when I don't want to do anything. They are trying to tell me Mirra that's what you have to do, so thanks for fighting with me and forcing me to do everything I have to do and not asking any questions."

Elina Svitolina fails to congratulate WTA Finals champion Mirra Andreeva

It was a lovely message from Andreeva, who continues to show real maturity beyond her years, both on and off the court. In contrast, Svitolina noticeably did not congratulate Andreeva in her speech. She has refused to shake hands with any Russian opponents and did so again at the end of this match.

However, it is worth noting the final speeches were done via an interview, and Svitolina was not directly asked a question about Andreeva. Her speech was as follows: "It was a great week for me and to be fair after the first match I was not expecting to play here in the final.

"Unfortunately it did not go my way but I gave it my all and I just want to say thank you so much for the support during this week and all the hard work. It was the last match of the season so it motivates me to go to pre-season and try my best next year."

And sharing a message for her daughter, the Ukrainian commented: "She is probably still awake and going to ask why I did not win today but I am really happy to be in great form and coming back after pregnancy.

"Hopefully it inspires some ladies and athletes around the world to believe it's possible. And I want to say thank you to people in Ukraine for supporting me and being on the journey with me."

Both WTA stars can be really proud of their efforts this week, and indeed their seasons overall. Andreeva will now finish her phenomenal 2026 season with four titles, including the French Open. Meanwhile, Svitolina clinched two titles in Auckland and Rome.

articles.title: Mirra Andreeva beats Elina Svitolina as she storms to WTA Finals title without dropping a set: 'It's something unbelievable'
articles.summary: Mirra Andreeva defeated Elina Svitolina 7-5 6-3 to win the WTA Finals; They were playing each other for the second time in the tournament after Andreeva's dominant win over Svitolina in the group stage; Svitolina was far more competitive in the final but could not derail the teenager
articles.body:
The Russian teenager, who laughed off being called a diva by rival Jessica Pegula in a 'hot mic' moment ahead of the tournament, did not drop a set on her singles debut at the season-ending showpiece, finishing with a 7-5 6-3 success.

At 19, the French Open champion is the first woman to claim the title before her 20th birthday since compatriot Maria Sharapova 22 years ago.

Andreeva had conceded only 18 games on route to the final, the fewest since the reintroduction of the round-robin format in 2003, with four of those coming in a dominant group win over Ukrainian Svitolina.

Their rematch in the final was much more competitive, with the pair, who are two of the best athletes in the sport, engaging in lengthy, lung-busting exchanges in intense rallies.

But Svitolina just could not get her nose in front and Andreeva finally served out the opening set at the second time of asking.

Svitolina, who won the title back in 2018, was grimly determined to hang on in the second set but Andreeva was strong, quick and unrelenting. The teenager jumped in the air with delight when Svitolina blasted an overarm smash into the net to concede the second match point.

Andreeva became the 11th player to win the Finals without losing a set, joining among others Chris Evert, Martina Navratilova and Serena Williams.

Andreeva, who will climb to second in the world rankings on Monday, told Sky Sports : "Coming into this match, it was the second time in my life that I thought I'm just going to die on the court but she's not getting the win.

"I'm going to have blisters, I'm going to have cramps, I'm going to have everything that you possibly can have, but I'm not going to lose this match.

"This spirit, this fighting mindset, just helped me to get through, helped me to get more brave and more aggressive in the important moments. It's crazy, something unbelievable. I'm so, so happy."

articles.title: WTA Finals: Mirra Andreeva beats Elina Svitolina to win season-ending title at Indian Wells
articles.summary: French Open champion Mirra Andreeva caps her stellar season with a hard-fought victory over Elina Svitolina to win the WTA Finals.
articles.body:
For Mirra Andreeva, the thought of her first WTA Finals singles campaign was so stressful that it gave her "a little breakdown" in a practice session before the tournament.

The 19-year-old may have been nervous on arrival at Indian Wells, but she leaves California as the champion, having been the standout player of the week.

The French Open winner produced a hard-fought 7-5 6-3 victory over Elina Svitolina in Sunday's final to become the youngest champion of the event in 22 years.

The Russian has now risen to second in the world rankings - and she will start the 2027 season just 293 points behind top-ranked Elena Rybakina.

Andreeva did not drop a set on her way to the title and lost only 26 games across her five matches.

She raised her arms in celebration after beating Svitolina before racing to celebrate with her team, which includes 1994 Wimbledon champion Conchita Martinez.

"I am super thankful to my team for pushing me to my limits, for forcing me to do stuff when I don't want to do anything," Andreeva said.

"Thanks for fighting with me, thanks for forcing me to do everything that I have to do and not asking any questions!"

As well as £2.55m in prize money, Andreeva also won a custom purple Mercedes - and joked she was happy to remain a "passenger princess" until she passed her test.

Andreeva thanks herself again after stellar season

One of the most notable parts of Andreeva's performance has been her increased maturity.

In March, she swore at the Indian Wells crowd after suffering an early defeat in the venue's WTA Tour tournament, and she has struggled to control her emotions , external on court in the past.

However, she showed little sign of that during this tournament.

Against Svitolina, one of the grittiest players on the women's tour, she lost a break lead three times across the two sets. Each time, she reset admirably, upping her aggression on her backhand in particular to put pressure back on her opponent.

After losing serve in a mammoth nine-minute game in the second set, Andreeva marched back to her chair and then broke Svitolina from 40-0 down in the next game to stay in front.

While her serve was not at its best, Andreeva still saved nine of the 12 break points she faced and hit 19 winners to Svitolina's 10.

"This fighting mindset helped me to get more brave and aggressive in the important moments," Andreeva told Sky Sports.

"This is just a dream. I had a little breakdown in my practice just before Indian Wells because I was so stressed.

"I didn't want to lose a match in the group. It's amazing."

Andreeva had only won one of her six matches against top-10 players in 2026 coming into the tournament.

She has beaten three top-10 players en route to the title, including a demolition of four-time major champion Aryna Sabalenka on Wednesday.

She also laughed off an incident before the tournament where private comments Jessica Pegula made to her coach about Andreeva - including calling her a "diva" - were live-streamed.

Just as she did when she won the French Open, Andreeva ended her speech by thanking herself - a twist on a quote she "stole" from rapper Snoop Dogg.

"I want to thank myself for always doing the hard work and for never quitting," she said.

"For not taking the days off, for working every day and committing to what I have to do - just thanks to myself."

'I want to thank myself' - Andreeva's journey to Grand Slam glory

Ukraine's Svitolina was tearful after the defeat, but reaching this stage capped a fine turnaround after she lost 6-4 6-0 to Andreeva on the first day of the tournament.

She pushed Andreeva throughout, drawing her into lengthy baseline rallies before fatigue set in.

She will finish the year at six in the world rankings, having made it back into the top 10 for the first time since 2021.

Svitolina returned from maternity leave in 2022, and joked that daughter Skai would have some questions for her after the match.

"She's probably still awake and is going to ask me why I didn't win today," the 32-year-old said.

"I'm really happy to be in great form and coming back after pregnancy. Hopefully it inspires some ladies and athletes around the world to believe that it's possible.

"I also want to say thank you to people in Ukraine for supporting me and being on this journey with me."

articles.title: Russia’s Andreeva defeats Ukraine’s Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 to win WTA Finals
articles.summary: Mirra Andreeva won the final in straight sets to end her first Grand Slam-winning year as world number two.
articles.body:
Russia’s teenage tennis star Mirra Andreeva has won her first WTA Finals crown without dropping a set against her Ukrainian rival Elina Svitolina, who did not shake hands with the champion at the end of a one-sided match in Indian Wells, California.

After her 7-5, 6-3 victory on Sunday, Andreeva, who turned 19 in April during a successful year that saw her win her first Grand Slam and ascend to number two in the world, took home $3.37m and a one-of-a-kind, ultraviolet purple Mercedes-Benz convertible car at the season-ending championships. Now, all she needs is a driver’s licence.

She happily got behind the wheel after the car was driven onto the court at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden.

“This is an amazing motivation for me to get my driver’s licence as fast as I can,” she said. “If not, then look, I have five people on my team. I’m going to be a passenger princess forever. That’s also an option for me.”

After match point, Andreeva ran to hug coach Conchita Martinez in the stands. Svitolina, a 32-year-old mother, sat down in her chair.

The players did not take part in the traditional post-match handshake or pose for photos together before the match. Svitolina and others from her country have refused to shake hands with players from Russia and Belarus since Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 in line with a policy set by the Ukrainian Tennis Federation.

Svitolina didn’t mention Andreeva in her post-match comments to the crowd, which included several fans waving Ukrainian flags.

Later, she said, “I couldn’t thank the people of Ukraine enough for coming to watch my matches, to watch at home.”

Andreeva publicly congratulated Svitolina for what she called an “amazing” season.

“You’re an amazing mom to come back and do this. It’s super hard,” she said. “I just wish you the best of luck for the next season.”

Svitolina nodded without expression from her seat.

“I put everything out there, and she played incredible,” Svitolina said later.

Andreeva became the 11th player to win the finals without losing a set, joining, among others, Chris Evert, Martina Navratilova and Serena Williams, all of whom did it multiple times.

“I’m super privileged to put my name in that group,” she said.

She jumped in the air when Svitolina netted an easy smash on the second match point.

Andreeva is also the second youngest player to win the WTA Finals behind her compatriot Maria Sharapova, who won at 17.

During the awards presentation, she wore a jacket with the phrase “I want to thank myself” stamped on the front, and then she did just that.

“I want to thank myself for always doing the hard work, for never quitting, for always believing in myself, for not taking the days off, for working every day and for committing to what I have to do,” she said. “Just thanks to myself without any reason.”

In doubles, Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend beat the Italian duo of Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini 6-4, 6-3.

It was the sixth title of the year for the Czech-American team of Siniakova and Townsend, who also won the French Open and US Open.

Svitolina said she would return to Ukraine next week, pledging to continue supporting her country through donations, her foundation and the platform she has built in tennis.

“It’s been almost five years. I’ve always been supportive of the army and the soldiers,” Svitolina told reporters. “They always support me by watching the matches, and I have lots of friends that are serving the country.”

Svitolina, the world number six, said sport could offer people a release from the strain and uncertainty of daily life during wartime.

“For me it’s all about the spirit, the spirit of the people,” she said. “I’m very happy that I can bring a little happiness to the people of Ukraine.”

“Sports in general and in Ukraine especially really unite people for one goal – to win.”

articles.title: Mirra Andreeva wins $3.37 million and specially customised Mercedes-AMG SL 55 bearing her name after WTA Finals victory at 19, but is yet to obtain her driving licence
articles.summary: 19-year-old Mirra Andreeva celebrates her WTA Finals victory with a record prize, customized Mercedes-AMG SL 55, and a rush to obtain her driving license.
articles.body: At 19, Mirra Andreeva has a new title, a record payday and the keys to a customised Mercedes-AMG sports car. There is just one small complication: the Russian teenager does not yet have a driving licence. Her breakthrough victory at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells has given her plenty to celebrate, although getting behind the wheel will have to wait.Andreeva takes home $3.37 million after unbeaten WTA Finals campaignAndreeva defeated Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in the singles final on November 15, completing an unbeaten run to win her maiden WTA Finals title. She did not drop a set across her five matches, earning the maximum singles champion's prize of $3.37 million (approximately ₹31.7 crore), along with the Billie Jean King Trophy and 1,500 ranking points.The tournament carried a total prize pool of $10 million, with $8 million allocated to singles and the remaining $2 million to doubles. Andreeva's earnings included her participation fee and the bonuses awarded for progressing through the competition. By winning every match, she secured the full amount available to an undefeated singles champion.The victory also lifted Andreeva to a career-high world No. 2 ranking, leaving her within 300 points of the top spot held by Elena Rybakina.Inside Andreeva's customised Mercedes-AMG SL 55The prize money was not the only reward waiting for Andreeva at the trophy presentation. She also received a one-off MANUFAKTUR Made to Measure Mercedes-AMG SL 55 4MATIC+, designed to celebrate the WTA Finals champion.Finished in an exclusive ultraviolet shade inspired by the WTA's signature purple, the roadster features 21-inch AMG forged wheels with a 10-twin-spoke design. Its interior combines crystal-white MANUFAKTUR Nappa leather with carbon trim and WTA Finals-inspired detailing. Other personalised touches include individually designed door sills, a badge bearing Andreeva's name and embossed headrest cushions.Under the bonnet, the SL 55 has a 4.0-litre V8 biturbo petrol engine, producing around 469-476 horsepower and 700 Nm of torque. It is paired with an AMG SPEEDSHIFT MCT nine-speed automatic transmission and Mercedes' 4MATIC+ all-wheel-drive system. The car can accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in 3.9 seconds.The convertible also comes with a lightweight fabric soft top, rear-axle steering and active ride control. Mercedes-Benz has not announced an official valuation for the specially commissioned vehicle.Why Andreeva cannot drive her new car just yetDespite receiving the keys on stage, Andreeva cannot legally take her new Mercedes out for a drive because she has yet to obtain her driving licence.She had previously joked that the players would not actually get the keys to the cars, making the presentation an especially welcome surprise. But I still want to just try to give it a little spin, maybe a couple of metres. I'm gonna be a passenger princess forever, so that's also an option for me," Andreeva said during the trophy ceremony.For now, her team may have to take turns behind the wheel. articles.standfirst: El murciano, luciendo estabilizador rotuliano, supera a Tiafoe en dos rápidos sets
articles.summary: El murciano, luciendo estabilizador rotuliano, supera a Tiafoe en dos rápidos sets
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz siempre fue un todoterreno y siempre le gustó la superficie rápida. La de Turín lo es, pero no tanto como la de París. Da igual, el murciano se ha autoconvencido de que tiene que hacer frente a cualquier tipo de adversidad. Al malestar en el estómago del viernes y las molestias en la rodilla desde su último torneo oficial en el Masters 1000 de la capital gala (juega con un estabilizador rotuliano) se le unía este lunes un teórico rival de entidad como Frances Tiafoe, vapuleado por 6-2 y 6-2, en 69 minutos. El estadounidense, octavo del ranking y uno de los cuatro debutantes en la cita de maestros, se inclinó ante un Carlitos superior contra él las últimas cinco temporadas. Es el intervalo de tiempo que pasó desde el único triunfo de Tiafoe en la primera ronda del Godó 2021. Alcaraz, que apenas llegaba al 70 por ciento de victorias bajo techo antes de Viena, está ya por encima del 75 por ciento de efectividad gracias a encadenar por primera vez en su carrera 11 partidos ganados en ese hábitat. Se mantiene invicto en superficie dura a cubierto en 2026. Ya son 38 triunfos, sólo superado en el curso por las 41 del ruso Daniil Medvedev, también presente en el grupo Ivan Lendl. El pupilo de Samuel López avisaba en la previa de su mayor seguridad al saque. La enseñó en el partido desde el primer juego. Cuatro puntos de servicio y dos 'aces'. Su víctima necesitó 10 puntos para anotarse uno al resto. Fue con un pasante de revés. Cada revés paralelo del campeón de siete grandes limpiaba la línea blanca. A los 14 minutos, el tanteo era de 4-0. Los aficionados que llenaban las 15.000 localidades del Inalpi Arena se decidieron por apoyar al americano. Para amortizar el precio de la entrada necesitaban más tenis. Frances levantaba los brazos a los 18 minutos tras estrenar su casillero. Se había salvado del rosco. El estadounidense, tras sumar dos juegos en la manga inicial, tomó la delantera en la continuación, con un 1-0. Esa fue su única alegría porque en el tercer juego encajaría un nuevo break. La derecha de Alcaraz iba como un cohete. Llegó a dispararla hasta los 165 kilómetros por hora. Nadie imaginaría que no la pegó durante cuatro meses y medio por el percance en la muñeca. Tener que levantar tres bolas de rotura en el sexto juego fue la mayor de sus preocupaciones. Tiafoe, amigo del fenómeno de El Palmar, llegó a pedirle clemencia en la red durante el último intercambio. Los cuatro juegos sumados son una losa para sus opciones de clasificación para las semifinales. Carlitos se sitúa líder destacado de su grupo y espera el miércoles al ganador del duelo entre Medvedev y Flavio Cobolli. El italiano ha llegado muy justo a Turín tras la lesión muscular que le obligó a abandonar en Viena con su compatriota Matteo Berrettini. Su anterior récord en indoor eran seis triunfos del tirón, entre las finales de la Copa Davis de 2024 y el torneo de Rotterdam 2025. Carlitos está a cuatro victorias de recortarle 6.090 puntos a Jannik Sinner en seis torneos. El italiano llegó a tener una diferencia de 6.440 tras que puede verse reducida a 350 puntos a finales de temporada. Y Sinner sigue convaleciente de la lesión de rodilla que le ha dejado fuera de la competición oficial desde Wimbledon.

articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz se congratulaba de su primera victoria en las ATP Finals de Turín 2026 y de su nivel de movilidad. Es una sensación muy bonita de tener y ojalá sigamos con este nivel". Invicto bajo techo. "Siempre he dicho que no soy malo en indoor y que otros eran un poco mejor que yo. Era cuestión de tiempo y de coger más experiencia. Entender cómo tenía que jugar en este tipo de pistas. Estoy contento de enseñarle a todo el mundo que puedo jugar un gran tenis aquí". Hago todo lo tengo que hacer fuera de la pista para estar en perfectas condiciones. Estoy intentando que la rodilla no me debe muchos problemas". Mejora en el servicio. "Samu es un crack". El objetivo del título. "En cada torneo siento que lo puedo ganar. Lo que uno piensa es lo más importante. Si vas a un torneo pensando que eres capaz de ganarlo, las probabilidades y la confianza aumenta. Si tú mismo no te dices cosas bonitas quién te las va a decir. Lo que no pienso es que sea el máximo favorito.
