articles.title: ATP Finals: Carlos Alcaraz begins title bid with statement win over Frances Tiafoe
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz warns his rivals he has never felt better at this stage of a season after beginning his ATP Finals bid with a statement win over Frances Tiafoe.
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz was at his scintillating best as his quest for a first ATP Finals triumph began with a statement victory over Frances Tiafoe.

Afterwards, the Spaniard warned his rivals that he has never felt better at this stage of the season.

Alcaraz hit 21 winners and made just nine unforced errors in a blistering 69-minute performance as he dismantled world number eight Tiafoe 6-2 6-2.

The seven-time major winner is on a 10-match winning streak following back-to-back titles in Vienna and Paris as he continues his remarkable return following a four-month wrist injury lay-off.

He has won three titles and lost just twice in 23 matches since making his return at the US Open in August.

"This is the best that I felt so far in my career at this part of the season," said the former world number one.

"I'm really happy with everything that I've done. I have obviously never experienced something like this year.

"It was unusual for me to have a lot of months out of competition and it means I'm coming here with a lot of energy and ambition."

Alcaraz takes revenge on Shelton to win first Paris Masters title

Zverev 'felt a lot of joy' in first win as world number one

Teenager Andreeva caps stunning week with WTA Finals title

Alcaraz reached the title match at the ATP Finals - the season-ending tournament featuring the year's eight top-performing men's players - for the first time last year.

On that occasion, he was beaten by main rival Jannik Sinner.

Having returned to full fitness, and with Sinner absent through injury, Alcaraz provided an immediate, ominous warning to his opponents on his return to Turin.

The 23-year-old lost just a single point on his serve and made only two unforced errors as he captured the first set in a devastating opening 27 minutes.

Tiafoe did not do an awful lot wrong, but the US Open semi-finalist was often left staring in bewilderment in response to his opponent's level.

The American maintained a first-serve average of 74%, but he was not able to win a single point on his second serve (0/12) during the match.

Dominant from the baseline, Alcaraz also dazzled with his athleticism and shot-making, while he showed necessary grit to deny Tiafoe three break points at 3-2 in the second set.

It was a performance scored as a 9.6 out of 10 by the ATP Performance Rating, which combines several statistics to measure a player's overall game.

"The trouble that I got every time I have played against Frances made me really focused," said Alcaraz, whose two most recent meetings with Tiafoe had come at Grand Slams and went to five sets.

"I prepared the match tactically really well. I wanted to let him know it was going to be a great battle if he wanted to win.

"I'm just really happy to start the tournament like this."

Home favourite Flavio Cobolli begins his tournament against Daniil Medevedev in the other Ivan Lendl Group match later on Monday.

articles.title: WTA chair Valerie Camillo says the Jessica Pegula-Mirra Andreeva incident at Indian Wells was 'not bad for viewership'
articles.summary: WTA chair Valerie Camillo discusses the hot mic moment at Indian Wells between Jessica Pegula and eventual champion Mirra Andreeva and the future of the body; You can watch the ATP Finals from Turin this week on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
Camillo personally apologised to Pegula , describing the broadcast of on-court conversations during a practice session at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells as "regrettable and unacceptable".

The Tour, who operated the livestream, had intended for the microphones to capture ambient sounds from the court but failed to inform participants.

A broadcast showed the American in conversation with her coach Mark Knowles, calling the 19-year-old a "diva" and saying she has lost respect for Andreeva's coach Conchita Martinez for not calling out her behaviour.

"Someone actually asked me if we planned it or did it on purpose to draw attention to the event," Camillo told Sky Sports' lead tennis commentator, Jonathan Overend.

"I wish that we were so crafty and strategic but we can't put ourselves in any situation where we put our athletes at risk. Our number one objective as a member services organisation for our players is to protect our players.

"What Jess said is competitive banter. I don't think there was anything particularly salacious in it. But having mics lying around that aren't being properly managed is not how the WTA expects to execute and operate.

"It created a viral moment. It created a lot of dialogue. But that's not intentional and not something you should expect to see us doing in the future.

"I've had this conversation here that I come from a variety of different sports. Before joining the WTA, I exclusively worked in male sports. I worked at the NBA and majorly baseball and it's quite common for there to be competitive banter that is brought into the forefront.

"It's up to the athletes for what they feel comfortable with and what they don't. But a little drama isn't bad for ticket sales.

"It's not bad for viewership. It's not bad for commentary. That's just a reality."

Andreeva laughed off the hot mic moment and went on to defeat Pegula 6-3 6-4 on Saturday, in a match that gained an extra layer of intrigue to reach the WTA Finals title match.

WTA finances and maximising financial opportunity

The WTA was forced to replace the venue for the season-ending event from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in July, which represented a major financial setback for the governing body.

The deal with the Saudi Tennis Federation (STF) included record prize money over a three-year period, but the ongoing tension between Iran and the United States made planning for the Finals more challenging, eventually forcing the tournament to move to Indian Wells in California.

The body is projecting operating losses of £17.3m ($23m) for 2026 and expects to hold roughly £11.3m ($15m) in cash by the end of the year, according to The Telegraph. Camillo remains confident of finding extra revenue streams through in-house media rights and sponsorship growth to create financial stability.

"Our ambition for the WTA Finals is equal prize money [with the men's tour]. That's our ambition, just as we expected of the Grand Slams. All of our combined 1000 events will have equal prize money in 2027," she said.

"We've been building fandom. We've been operating globally. We've been creating superstar athletes through our platform for many, many decades, and so the athletes have the opportunity not to just earn on the court, but also to control their own brands and monetise that off the court.

"WTA intends to remain in its position as number one in the hearts and minds of fans, in the mindset and investment of our sponsors, and we want to be building an even greater platform on which our great athletes can compete, not only one that they can enjoy from the ferocity of the crowd, but also one that enables them to maximise their financial opportunity to the best of our ability."

WTA intends to have 'better controls' of revenue streams

One of the WTA revenue streams comes from selling data, match data, court feeds to data companies with the betting industry a large part of that.

Burrage, who was playing her first WTA Tour match since Wimbledon last summer, received death threats and online abuse following a first-round defeat at a tournament in India .

The 27-year-old shared a raft of abusive messages sent to her Instagram account. Alongside the video, Burrage wrote: "Nice welcome back to the tour. I remember why I left."

Camillo said: "The complexity of official data to these partners is sort of an industry inside thing. But the reality is that through having official partnerships, you actually can have more integrity and controls.

"If you don't have relationships with these variety of platforms, you can turn into a little bit of the wild, wild west. It's not to say that there isn't a financial element to these relationships. That would be disingenuous. Of course there is. But it does also enable us to have a partnership that leads to better controls."

articles.title: Henry Patten: British doubles No 1 takes swipe at ATP chairman and CEO for absence from trophy presentation
articles.summary: Henry Patten uses trophy presentation to focus on the absence of ATP bosses, reigniting his opposition to the doubles reform expected for 2028; You can watch the ATP Finals in Turin this week on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
Upon receiving the year-end doubles No 1 trophy from chief tour officer Andre Silva, alongside his Finnish partner Harri Heliovaara, Patten called out the ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi and CEO Eno Polo.

"For us, it's a really big deal. It's a real shame that the ATP chairman and CEO don't think the same." Patten said.

"It would have been nice to have them on court with us today, but here we are by ourselves."

Sky Sports News has contacted the ATP Tour for comment.

Patten and Heliovaara enjoyed a sensational season, winning Wimbledon for the second time in their careers and lifting trophies in Adelaide, Doha, Dubai, and Madrid.

The duo have repeatedly criticised the ATP's approach to doubles, including their proposals that would include smaller draws and reduce prize money for the 2028 season.

Patten and Dutch player Sem Verbeek spearheaded an open letter, signed by over a hundred other players - including former champions Bob and Mike Bryan - calling for the reform project to be scrapped.

Speaking to Sky Sports Tennis , Tim Henman said: "He [Patten] made his thoughts pretty clear about the lack of representation from the chair and the CEO on the tour.

"There is the conversation around massive reform in the doubles world, potentially cutting the doubles draw in half and that would save prize money that could go into the singles, so those doubles players are feeling like their jobs are in jeopardy.

"This is a great platform as the doubles is getting incredible support."

Heliovaara also addressed the crowd, thanking Patten and their team, saying: "I'm going to say that Henry is the best partner in the world for doubles. I've been lucky enough to play with him for two and a half years.

"We shared a lot of wins, a lot of losses, but most of all, a lot of time everywhere in the world, really. On the court, off court, it's been a very nice, amazing trip together. But it's not just the two of us, I think it's also our team there in the box, in the spotlight today.

"I would like that we also give a big hand to every one of them. It's a lot of sacrifices from us, from the team, and obviously our families at home. Everybody who has helped us to achieve something like this. And to have a trophy like that at home, we will be very proud for a very long time."

Patten and Heliovaara will now turn their attention to the task at hand in Turin, where they are 1-0 in round-robin play. They defeated Orlando Luz and Rafael Matos in a match tie-break on Sunday.

articles.standfirst: El estadounidense perdió los 12 puntos con su segundo servicio, algo que no pasaba desde Estoril 2012
articles.summary: El estadounidense perdió los 12 puntos con su segundo servicio, algo que no pasaba desde Estoril 2012
articles.body: Normal que Frances Tiafoe llegara a tomárselo casi a coña porque la superioridad de Carlos Alcaraz fue insultante. "Al menos no voy a perder 0 y 0", dijo el estadounidense tras ganar su primer juego. El doble 6-2 final no deja lugar a dudas pero tampoco es un marcador escandaloso. Lo que no fue nada normal fue una estadística que hacía nada menos que 14 años que no se veía en el circuito ATP... Hablamos de la efectividad al resto del murciano con el segundo servicio de Tiafoe. El estadounidense metió el 74% de sus primeros saques y con ellos ganó el 74% de los puntos (26 de 35). Hasta aquí nada reseñable y, de hecho, no difiera casi nada de lo que hizo Carlitos, que ganó el 78% de sus primeros saques (28 de 36). La 'salvajada' del tenista de El Palmar llegó con el segundo servicio de Tiafoe. Doce puntos que fueron cayendo de forma inmisericorde en favor del español, que en las mismas circunstancias ganó 8 de los 10 que disputó. Esto significa que Alcaraz fue aún más mortífero con su segundo saque (80%) que con el primero. Ese 0-12 de Tiafoe es un 'perro verde' en el mundo del tenis. Una estadística tan inusual que no se veía en el circuito ATP desde 2012. En concreto desde un partido de segunda ronda en el torneo de Estoril entre el argentino Juan Martín del Potro y el portugués Rui Machado. Ese día, a comienzos de mayo, el genial y espigado tenista del Tandil le endosó un 6-1, 6-0 al luso, que no pudo ganar ninguno de los diez puntos que jugó con su segundo saque. Es más, Del Potro, cabeza de serie número 1 del torneo, acabaría levantando el trofeo sin ceder un solo set. Sin duda un estupendo precedente para Alcaraz aunque en Turín, qué duda cabe, aún queda mucha tela que cortar y las ATP Finals no son un ATP 250...

articles.title: 'All of us are going to be accountable': AITA vice-presidential candidate Leander Paes on his vision
articles.summary: New Delhi: After opting not to contest for the All India Tennis Association (AITA) president's post, Leander Paes filed his nomination for the
articles.body: New Delhi: After opting not to contest for the All India Tennis Association (AITA) president's post, Leander Paes filed his nomination for the vice-president's role on Monday, the last date of nominations for the elections scheduled for November 27. The 53-year-old has backed the interim AITA president Chintan Parikh, as part of a group called 'Tennis First'.Paes, who represented India at seven Olympics, winning a bronze in 1996, said his priority was to focus on grassroots wile making every individual and every state association accountable."There is a lot that I can learn from Chintan bhai where my first foot into sports administration, governance, I need to learn. His vision for Indian tennis, for AITA, to clean up the system is a wonderful vision. Where I feel I can be asset to the team is in grassroot development, player development, empowering the sport, funding the AITA and empowering the state associations to empower the players," he told select reporters on Monday."Our vision is a very clean AITA with a focus on the players. Grassroots development is the bottom one to scholarships for talented children in rural areas. Tennis is still considered an affluent sport, one for the elite.""The first step is to clean it up (the corruption). The second step is to build the grassroots, then get the funding in, empower the state associations who empower the players," he continued.Paes didn't shy away from hitting out at the previous administration of AITA and the alleged misuse of funds under their term. The 20-time Grand Slam winner added that the alleged misuse of administrative positions for personal gains had damaged AITA's reputation. Subsequently, it made Indian tennis less attractive to corporate sponsors.The first step is to clean it up (the corruption). The second step is to build the grassroots, then get the funding in, empower the state associations who empower the players"It is not difficult to put a professional system in place. But it has to be an ideology. It has to be a practised craft. When you have a system where personal gains come into play, nothing can be professional. Personal gains when people take the funding and misuse it. Personal gains when they think that a trust fund [AITA Trust Fund] is their own personal fund. When public tax hard-earned money comes into an association and is played by a few individuals. How can it be professional?"So what we are planning to do behind the scenes is to bring a professional legal team. So that starting with Leander Paes, Chintan Parikh ji, Sundar Iyer, the rest of the whole team there will be a Code of Conduct. There will be transparency. The transparency goes not just on AITA but also into state and for individuals. All of us must be transparent," continued Paes.Paes stressed it was important for AITA, and many other National Sports Federations (NSFs), to be inspired by the BCCI and learn from them. He used examples of the IPL, the U-19s, and women's cricket as categories which have grown, not just the men's team.Paes, who holds the record for most doubles wins in Davis Cup history, acknowledged the role some of his peers will have to play in bolstering Indian tennis, despite a controversy-laden trajectory with some of them.He vowed to work closely with Mahesh Bhupathi, Sania Mirza, Rohan Bopanna, the Sports Authority of India (SAI) and the Sports Ministry in developing the next generation."See, I have dealt with these challenges for 40 years. Same human beings, same characters, same positions. But different capacity this time. As far as I am concerned, the playing field just changes. Before it was playing, now it is administration," claimed Paes."Rohan, Mahesh, Sania. Why only three of them? Why not Somdev Devvarman? Why not Purav Raja? Why not other great players that have played Asian Games, won medals? Why not Radhika Tulpule? Why not Janaki (Krishnamoorthy)? Why not Rushmi (Chakravarthi)? Why not Vishal Uppal? There are so many players there beyond Leander, Mahesh, Sania and Rohan, there are many other players who have dedicated their lives to tennis. They must be empowered also.I'm going to be accountable to my position and what I'm doing. Likewise, everybody is accountable. It's not going to be a worry at all."Working with these players is not a problem at all. Mahesh and I are very different human beings but what we've achieved together is huge. Sania and myself, we've won golds together. Rohan and myself have done great Davis Cup together. So I feel it's a sense of respect, professionalism and inclusiveness to make a healthy organisation."Now, all of us are going to be accountable. I'm going to be accountable to my position and what I'm doing. Likewise, everybody is accountable. It's not going to be a worry at all. We all know each other really well. I'm sure there'll be some sticky wickets. I'm sure there'll be some tough conversations. And at the end of the day, the sport must win. The sport is bigger than every human being in the world," finished Paes.Nominations for AITA ElectionsPresident: Rohit Rajpal, Chintan ParikhVice-president: Prashant Sutar, Leander PaesSecretary General: Gurucharan Singh, Sunder IyerJoint Secretary (Male): Sunil Yajaman, Sumit GoelJoint Secretary (Female): Prerna BhambriTreasurer: Asit Tripathy, Sujit RoyExecutive Committee: Velmati Narayndas, Krishna Kumar Singh, B Venkatasubramanyam, PV Rama Kumar, Ankush Dutta, Malsawm Dawngi, Chetan Kapur, Madhurjya Sarmah, BS JaggiAthletes Commission: Yuki Bhambri, Rutuja Bhosale, Sravya Shivani ChilakalapudiGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tennis: Britain's Henry Patten criticises ATP chairman and CEO for trophy presentation absence
articles.summary: Britain's top-ranked doubles player Henry Patten criticises the ATP's chairman and CEO for missing the year-end world number one trophy presentation.
articles.body:
Britain's top-ranked doubles player Henry Patten criticised the ATP's chairman and CEO for their absence at Monday's year-end world number one trophy presentation.

Wimbledon champions Patten and Finnish team-mate Harri Heliovaara received their trophy ​from the ATP's chief tour officer Andre Silva in Turin, after ending the season as the top-ranked men's doubles pairing for the first time.

In his acceptance speech, Patten, 30, called out ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi and CEO ​Eno Polo for their decision not to attend.

"What a journey it has been. Turin is such a special place for us, we played a challenger just across the road when we ranked 60 and 40 in the world a couple of years ago. I never would ​have dreamt that we would be in the position that we're in now," said Patten.

"For ​us it's a really big deal. ​It's a real shame that the ATP ‌chairman ⁠and the ATP CEO don't think the same.

"It would have been nice to have them on ​court with ​us ⁠today, but here we are by ourselves.

"We have worked incredibly hard and thank you all for appreciating that."

BBC Sport has contacted ​the ATP Tour for comment.

Angry players urge ATP rethink over doubles cuts

It is crystal clear why Patten decided he needed to dig out ATP bosses Gaudenzi and Polo.

Patten, Heliovaara and the rest of the men's doubles cohort believe their governing body simply does not care about their discipline.

And, as Patten barely concealed in his pointed speech, the non-appearance of Gaudenzi and Polo underlined what the players believe is a lack of respect.

In July, the ATP made proposals to halve doubles draws at its flagship Masters 1000 events to 16 teams. Smaller tournaments would be reduced to eight teams.

That would see the percentage of prize money devoted to doubles events falling from 20% to 10%, with the difference redistributed to singles players.

The plans drew the fury of doubles players, who believe the "drastic" changes could kill the format . Patten also used his Wimbledon victory speech to passionately point out the importance of doubles.

The ATP says it wants to create "a more sustainable long-term model" for the men's tour, insisting it wants to "maintain the important role" of doubles.

The tour's board - comprised of chairman Gaudenzi, four tournament representatives and four player representatives - will vote on the plans in Turin this week.

Gaudenzi and Polo are spending much of their week in those meetings.

The decision will shape the future of men's doubles, along with the careers and lives of its players.

By speaking out again now, Patten's barbed comments were interpreted to be timely, in an attempt to apply more pressure before the ATP board meets on Tuesday and Wednesday.

articles.title: Álex Corretja: "Siento que este es el año de Alcaraz, tengo el 'feeling' de que ha llegado el momento"
articles.standfirst: El barcelonés, campeón del torneo de maestros en 1998, está en Turín liderando el equipo de Movistar Plus
articles.summary: El barcelonés, campeón del torneo de maestros en 1998, está en Turín liderando el equipo de Movistar Plus
articles.body: El tenis masculino español, que se ha acostumbrado a ganar cada año títulos del Grand Slam, primero con Rafael Nadal y después con Carlos Alcaraz, sigue costándole triunfar en las ATP Finals. Desde la primera edición del torneo en 1970 tan sólo dos títulos: Manolo Orantes (1976) y Álex Corretja (1998). Este último, presente en Turín liderando las retransmisiones de Movistar Plus, se sienta con MARCA. Pregunta. ¿Por qué sólo se ha ganado dos veces el Masters masculino? Respuesta. La superficie influye mucho. Nosotros hemos crecido jugando con parábola , en tierra... Nuestra esencia no es la pista cubierta. No es sólo pensar que el saque es lo más importante. No es pensar que tienes que pegar un golpe paralelo parra ganar el punto. Los españoles tenemos un juego muy psicológico a la vez que físico. Las ATP Finals se juegan en noviembre y llegamos bastante triturados. Ferru hizo final, Juanki, Rafa... Pero el juego de Nadal no era tan efectivo aquí como en otras superficies. En rápida al aire libre o incluso en hierba no le importaba mucho porque al ser zurdo tenía claro cómo tenía que jugar. El Masters es como un híbrido, que no sabes si ir para atrás o para adelante. Mi final con Moyá fue algo muy raro, pero es verdad que en la pista de Hannover la pelota botaba muy alta si lo comparamos con lo que nos encontramos en indoor habitualmente. La mayoría de los jugadores que clasifican han crecido en rápida, dígase Djokovic, Federer, Sampras, Agassi... P. ¿Tanta diferencia hay entre dura al aire libre respecto a la pista cubierta? R. Sí que la hay porque en indoor no hay viento y eso favorece a los sacadores. No molesta el sol. La pelota no bota tan alta y eso se nota también si juegas sesión de día o de noche al aire libre. Jugar de noche en un outdoor es lo más parecido al indoor, tienes la sensación de que no haces mucho daño al rival. En nuestro tenis los efectos son muy importantes y con techo se limitan bastante. La suerte para Alcaraz es que él ha crecido en otra generación y ha entrenado mucho en rápida. P. ¿Siente que es el año de Carlitos, por cómo llega y por las ausencias de Novak Djokovic y Jannik Sinner? R. Teniendo en cuenta que ellos dos no están y también analizando la temporada de Carlos. No hay mal que por bien no venga. Al estar tantos meses fuera ha llegado más fresco a este torneo. Ha ganado partidos en Viena y París y eso le ha dado el ritmo y la confianza que él necesitaba. Antes llegaba aquí y daba la sensación que estaba incómodo un poco con todo. Cansado, saturado mentalmente, a nivel tenístico veías que a veces se iba muy para atrás, no sabía si tirar liftado... Ahora ha entendido lo que tiene que hacer. Con lo bien que se mueve y lo bien que le pega, su variedad, no hay motivos para que no ofrezca su mejor tenis aquí. Mi sensación es que este es el año de Alcaraz por cómo se ha dado todo. Tengo el feeling de que ha llegado el momento. Otros compañeros han estado cerca. Tanto Orantes como yo estaríamos felices de que Carlos ganara. Ya nos hubiera encantado que hubiese sido Rafa. Si Alcaraz gana el Masters es mejor para todos. A mí no me van a quitar el título. Simplemente habrá otro jugador después de mí que lo habrá ganado. A mí que digan que Álex Corretja ha sido el último español no me aporta. Yo he comentado todas las grandes finales, Copa Davis, medallas olímpicas, Grand Slam, todas las entrevistas después de los partidos... La única entrevista que no he hecho es la del Masters y la quiero hacer. Es como cerrar un círculo como comentarista. Con Nadal me hubiera gustado, pero que sea Alcaraz para mí es una motivación bonita. Y me motivaría igual que fuera Jódar, pero acaba de llegar y lo veo más difícil. P. ¿Haber ganado en Viena y París hace que Alcaraz se lo crea más? R. Muchísimo más. Sin intentar compararlo, yo gané en Lyon antes de Hannover y ya supe que podía ganar un torneo en indoor. Si Carlos está fresco físicamente es muy complicado pararlo. Eso no quiere decir que vaya a ganar fácil. Mentalmente lo veo muy maduro y preparado. P. ¿Es un premio para Rafa Jódar estar aquí? R. Lo de Jódar no se puede entender y tiene un mérito incalculable. Un chaval que hace un año estaba el 170 del mundo , que viaja solo con su padre, lo que han hecho, cómo lo han gestionado, cómo ha mejorado en todas las superficies... Es que cada partido que pasa da la sensación de que progresa. Como dirían los ingleses es un fast learner, es un chico que aprende rápido. Y es un killer y lo está demostrando. Lo que ha conseguido sólo con su padre es para sacarse el sombrero. La lógica dice que el año que viene empiecen a incorporar a gente al equipo . Eso no quiere decir que tengan que ser ocho más. Cuando más bueno eres más necesitas a un equipo detrás. Yo creo que acabarán incorporando a alguien, ya sea a nivel tenístico para asesorar algunas semanas, algún fisio, preparador físico... Tienen que encontrar a alguien que entienda la filosofía de Rafa, del padre, porque son un grupo muy cerrado. Tienen que estar seguros de que, el que se incorpore, le haga una ilusión increíble el proyecto. No pueden coger a alguien sólo por el caramelo de ayudar a Jódar. Entonces sería interés y no ilusión. P. Del baile en los banquillos qué me dice. Por ejemplo la únión de Juan Carlos Ferrero con Ben Shelton. ¿Le ha sorprendido? R. No me esperaba que fuera Shelton, me esperaba, por supuesto, que fuera alguien con potencial para ganar un Grand Slam. Yo creo que les va a ir muy bien porque Shelton está en un momento de plena madurez y Juanki le puede aportar muchas cosas. El padre de Ben es un trozo de pan y estoy seguro de que se compenetrarán muy bien. Shelton tiene mucho margen de mejora en cuanto a orden, en cuanto a táctica, entender lo que es el juego y está dispuesto a hacerlo. No tengo dudas de que acabarán triunfando en los grandes. Si a mi me dicen si apuesto a que van a ganar un título de Grand Slam yo apuesto a que sí. Ya lo dije hace un año en una de las encuestas que hacemos en la tele, pero ahora lo veo más claro que nunca. P. ¿Y la relación entre David Ferrer y Casper Ruud? R. Es una relación muy positiva para los dos porque son tranquilos, educados, ambiciosos y sin tener el foco del 'top3' o 'top4'. Casper todavía tiene juego y las ganas, y en Roland Garros no hay tantos jugadores a cinco sets y en tierra que sean capaces de ganarle. La combinación con el padre y Pedro seguro que será buena. Yo estoy muy contento tanto por Ferrero como por Ferrer. El único que echo de menos en el circuito es a Moyá. Alguien como él tiene que estar vinculado al tenis porque es un legado nuestro que a de continuar. Cada uno ha ido encontrando su sitio. Yo, en mi caso, intento transmitirlo de la mejor manera posible en la tele. Moyá, junto a Rafa, que está a otro nivel, estaría bien que estuviera en el circuito porque es un referente. Me gustaría que ayudara a un jugador aunque fuera 10 semanas al año, pero depende de él. P. ¿Usted se echa de menos en el circuito o su etapa como técnico se ha acabado? R. Yo he tenido y tengo ofertas de jugadores y realmente 'tops'. Pero mi vida profesional y personal está bien encaminada. Me siento muy a gusto de cómo me tratan tanto en Eurosport como en Movistar Plus, al igual que en el resto de medios. A nivel familiar la vida que tengo es mucho más práctica que estar detrás de un jugador. Y combinar ser asesor de alguien con los medios no la veo, hago una cosa o la otra. Tengo dos años más firmados con Movistar Plus y otros dos con Eurosport. Cuando acabe en 2028 ya veré qué hago con mi vida profesional.

articles.title: A Rafa Jódar le pasan factura los 80 partidos a sus espaldas y está con un pie fuera de las ATP Finals
articles.standfirst: El madrileño cede en tres sets ante Fils y depende de otros para seguir vivo en el torneo
articles.summary: El madrileño cede en tres sets ante Fils y depende de otros para seguir vivo en el torneo
articles.body: Rafa Jódar no ha podido convertirse este martes en el decimosegundo tenista español capaz de ganar un partido del Masters masculino. Ha cedido ante Arthur Fils, por 4-6, 6-2 y 6-2, en 1 hora y 52 minutos. Se quedaron con las ganas de estrenar su casillero de victorias en la cita de maestros Andrés Gimeno, Emilio Sánchez Vicario, Alberto Berasategui, Fernando Verdasco y Pablo Carreño. El madrileño aún tiene la oportunidad de sumar el primer triunfo este jueves en la última jornada del grupo John McEnroe ante Ben Shelton. Su futuro en el torneo está en manos del estadounidense. Si Ben gana a Alexander Zverev, en el cierre del día, estará eliminado. El número cuatro mundial ya no contará con la ayuda de Juan Carlos Ferrero, que abandonó Turín el lunes porque tenía compromisos adquiridos previamente en Asia. Jódar se anotó los seis primeros puntos del partido. Fils, una fuerza de la naturaleza, reaccionó a pelotazo limpio. Era un duelo entre dos de los cuatro debutantes del torneo, que aspiraban a ser el más joven nacido en 2004 o más adelante en sumar un triunfo en la cita de maestros. Arthur, de 22 años, contra Rafa, de 20. El de Leganés dominaba los precedentes por dos victorias a una. Jódar se agarró a su servicio (con puntas de 215 kilómetros por hora) para salvar las dos primeras pelotas de break del adversario en el tercer juego. Levantó una tercera, con 4-4. Al jugador del Chamartín le costaba ajustar con su tiro de derecha. Fueron suyas las dos primeras bolas de set en el décimo parcial. Aprovechó la segunda. El galo falló en el momento de máxima presión, algo habitual. Un largo intercambio acabó con una bola de Fils a la red. Rafa Jódar senior aprovechaba el descanso para repasar las estadísticas y sacar sus conclusiones. Fils volvió a escena con una doble rotura en el tercer y quinto juego de la continuación. Al joven español le había dado un bajón físico y pidió la presencia del fisioterapeuta, con 4-1. Se tomó algo y siguió jugando, pero su lenguaje corporal no era el mejor. Hacía saber de su malestar a su padre, presente en la primera fila del Inalpi Arena porque es también su entrenador. "Apóyate bien en el suelo cuando golpees", le decía a su hijo. Este volvió a perder su servicio en el tercer juego de la manga de desempate. No parecía con fuerzas de firmar una remontada. Los 80 partidos jugados en su primera campaña como profesional pasan factura. Y aún le falta como mínimo uno más en Turín y un máximo de tres en la fase final de la Copa Davis de Bolonia. Fils se convierte en el primer tenista de su país en ganar un partido de las ATP Finals desde 2011.

articles.title: ATP Finals: Alexander Zverev books place in semi-finals after brushing aside Ben Shelton; Arthur Fils beats Rafael Jodar
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev beat Ben Shelton in straight sets to book his place in the knockout stages of the ATP Finals; Rafael Jodar will not progress past the groups after he suffered defeat to Arthur Fils; watch the ATP Nitto Finals live on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
His victory means debutant Rafael Jodar will not advance to the semi-finals after the Spaniard suffered defeat to Zverev in their opening match of the tournament, before being bested 4-6 6-2 6-2 by Arthur Fils earlier in the day.

Zverev, whose service game was impeccable against Shelton, will jump to the top of the John McEnroe Group standings, having not dropped a set so far during the tournament, as he swept away the American to bring up a flawless 7-0 winning record against the 24-year-old.

"I think for me, if I focus on myself and play good tennis, the results will take care of themselves in a way," Zverev said after the match.

"The results are not what I focus on, it's about playing good tennis, and I felt like I did that today, and I did that against Rafa [Rafael Jodar] two days ago.

Shelton dropped to a record of 1-1 and will likely need to win his final group match against Jodar to advance to the semi-finals, with Fils also sitting at 1-1.

Zverev came out of the blocks quickly, breaking Shelton in the first game of the match, before following up with a second to go 4-1 up, and would see out the first set from there.

As the German looked to advance, Shelton responded, forcing Zverev to a tiebreak in the second set, but the world No 1 was too strong, outmuscling his opponent with a clinical forehand back down the American's left tramline to seal victory.

'He's looking very comfortable as the new No 1'

"From Zverev's point of view, it's looking very routine. It's not as if Zverev is hitting 'wonder-shots'.

"The serve is doing such a good job of consistently hitting the spots and getting so many cheap points and holding serve from the back of the court.

"He is more aggressive, he's moving the ball around, and he played smart tennis as well, and he moved forward at the right time.

"He's looking very comfortable and confident as this new world No 1."

Fils claimed his first win at the ATP Finals by rallying past fellow debutant Jodar in three sets.

The Frenchman, like Shelton, now needs a big result against top-ranked Zverev in his final group match to advance to the semi-finals.

Jodar, meanwhile, appeared to be struggling physically midway through the second set and was given medicine to mix into his water bottle during a medical timeout. He also devoured a banana, a gel and an energy bar during the next changeover.

The 20-year-old is the first man to qualify for the year-end finals in the same season in which he made his tour-level debut. He has appeared fatigued recently.

"I felt that I couldn't compete," Jodar said.

"Physically, I wasn't at the level today, especially in the last two sets.

articles.title: Leo Borg carries Bjorn Borg's legendary tennis legacy: How the Swedish star is overcoming family expectations, public pressure and comparisons while building his own professional career
articles.summary: Explore how Leo Borg is navigating the pressures of his father's legendary tennis career while building his own path in professional sports. Discover his journey, achievements, and aspirations in the world of tennis.
articles.body: Leo Borg’s professional tennis career is a unique challenge for few young players. Most up-and-coming players are concerned with moving up the rankings, building their games and earning opportunities on the tour, but the 23-year-old Swede must also deal with the expectations of his famous surname. His father, Bjorn Borg, one of the most famous players in tennis history, picked up 11 Grand Slam singles titles during an outstanding career.Leo has lived with the pressure of being such a successful sporting figure since his junior days. But the young tennis player has always emphasized how important it is to work on his own development and not try to repeat his father’s successes. His rise through the junior ranks, ITF events and ATP tournaments mirrors a sustained attempt to forge a professional identity on his own terms.How Leo Borg builds a tennis career beyond Bjorn BorgAs the son of an international tennis legend, it opens doors but has also faced a fair bit of public scrutiny. The challenge for Leo Borg has been striking a balance between paying tribute to his father’s accomplishments while making sure his own performances are noticed.Between 1976 and 1980, Borg won the French Open six times and the Wimbledon championship five times in a row. His achievements were so great that the Borg name became synonymous with tennis greatness, so it was inevitable that comparisons would be made when Leo decided to play the same sport.In an interview with the International Tennis Federation in March 2021, Leo admitted that people often judged him based on what his father had achieved rather than on what he had achieved himself. But he also said he was starting to see a shift as his tennis improved and crowds started to take more notice of his individual results.Bjorn Borg supports Leo Borg's independenceBjorn Borg has remained involved in his son’s tennis journey, but is not trying to be his chief coach. The former world No. 1 has opted to let Leo work with his own coaching team and make independent decisions about his professional career, rather than directly managing every facet of his development.This strategy has enabled Leo to create a training environment tailored to his individual needs. During his junior development, he spent time at the Rafa Nadal Academy in Spain before returning to the Royal Tennis Club in Stockholm to continue working with coach Rickard Billing.The deal accepts that Leo has to develop his own strengths, instead of just copying the ways that made his father successful. Though Bjorn’s experience is a valuable source of guidance, the younger Borg is free to shape his training, competitive approach, and ambitions independently.Leo Borg's progress on the professional tourLeo’s professional development has hit some key milestones, but not at the same speed as his father’s. He caught early attention in junior competitions and then slowly gained experience against more established professional players.One of his best junior results came in 2021 when he won the boys’ singles at the tournament in Porto Alegre, Brazil. The win was an important step forward and helped cement his position among the promising young players.He also made news at the junior Wimbledon championships and won his first-round match in the 2021 French Open boys’ singles tournament. These appearances contributed to the attention that was due to the historical connection between his father and the Grand Slam tournaments.He has since turned pro, playing in ATP and ITF World Tennis Tour events. According to ATP Tour coverage published in April 2025, Leo got a shot to play qualifying at the Barcelona Open Banc Sabadell, a tournament his father won in 1975 and 1977. He was beaten in straight sets by Britain’s Jacob Fearnley, but the appearance was another chance to get experience at a higher level.Leo Borg's ATP results and career milestonesThe Swede’s career has seen him get to test himself against seasoned pros and get a taste of life on the ATP Tour. It was a big personal moment, although he didn't make it past the opening round, as Nadal had been one of his biggest inspirations growing up.Leo played in the BNP Paribas Nordic Open in Stockholm and had another opportunity to show the progress he has made to a home crowd.He had a good win against Sebastian Ofner at the Stockholm tournament in 2025. The outcome showed he could hold his own against players with far more experience on the pro circuit. ATP statistical records also show a career-high singles ranking of No 334, which was achieved in September 2023.Despite the hype around his family background, Leo has managed to maintain lofty aspirations for his professional future. His rise has required patience, not least because moving from junior tournaments to the senior circuit is a massive step up in terms of physical, technical and competitive demands.Leo spoke in September 2025 about expectations associated with his surname while discussing his father’s autobiography and his recovery from illness. He acknowledged that the pressure had felt greater when he was younger but said he had gotten better at adapting to expectations. He also made it clear that his career was still his own.The young Swede insisted that his ultimate ambition was still to break into the world’s top 10, although he accepted that he was slightly disappointed at the lack of speed in his progress. He also said he was confident in his ability and the potential he felt was still there in his game.Why comparisons with Bjorn Borg remain unavoidableThe two Leos and Bjorn will probably continue to be compared because of their common surname, Swedish nationality, and participation in professional tennis. But their careers are being played in different competitive environments, with the demands of modern tennis requiring different physical preparation, playing strategies, and consistency.He built his legacy on 11 Grand Slam singles titles, including his incredible run at Wimbledon and the French Open. Meanwhile, Leo is still in the early stages of his professional career and has yet to achieve similar success at the highest level.The younger Borg has also spoken about Rafael Nadal being his biggest tennis inspiration rather than just going by his father’s playing history. His love for Nadal shows that his sporting inspirations extend beyond his family background.Leo is only 23, so he still has time to develop his game and go after his dreams. articles.title: ATP Finals: Arthur Fils beats Rafael Jodar for first win
articles.summary: Rising star Arthur Fils claims his first career win at the ATP Finals by battling to a comeback victory over Rafael Jodar to remain in contention in Turin.
articles.body:
Rising star Arthur Fils claimed his first career win at the ATP Finals by battling to a comeback victory over Rafael Jodar to remain in contention in Turin.

Fils, 22, beat 20-year-old Jodar 4-6 6-2 6-2 to become the first Frenchman to record an ATP Finals victory since Jo-Wilfried Tsonga in 2011.

It was the youngest match by combined age at the season-ending tournament - which features the eight top-performing men - since a 21-year-old Novak Djokovic defeated a 20-year-old Juan Martin del Potro in 2008.

Fils has risen to a career-high ranking of seventh in the world during a season in which he became the youngest French ATP Masters 1000 champion in Cincinnati.

All four debutants at this year's tournament lost their opening match, with Fils beaten by American third seed Ben Shelton and Spain's Jodar losing to Alexander Zverev in the John McEnroe Group.

But Fils, a finalist at the Next Gen ATP Finals three years ago, will fight for a place in the semi-finals against world number one Zverev on Thursday after keeping alive his hopes of reaching the knockout stage on his debut.

"It's going to be tough but I know that I can battle. I'm not afraid," said Fils of his showdown with Zverev, who plays Shelton later on Tuesday.

"It will be a nice match against the world number one. I don't have anything to lose, I'm just going to enjoy myself."

Superb Alcaraz makes statement start at ATP Finals

GB's Patten criticises ATP chairman and CEO for absence

Fils was second best in the first set but gradually found his rhythm to outperform a fading Jodar over sets two and three.

Jodar made an ideal start, striking at the perfect moment when he broke for the first time to clinch the opening set after 10 games.

Fils particularly struggled on serve, landing just 38% of first serves in, and produced just a single winner in a flat first set.

But the Frenchman reset impressively in the second, twice breaking Jodar's serve on his way to forcing a decider.

Jodar appeared to be fading physically and took a medical timeout after falling a double break behind in the second set.

The Spaniard was unable to rediscover his previous level, however, and Fils powered to victory by winning six of the final seven games.

"It means a lot to me after a tough start," Fils said.

"I played a great game against Ben [Shelton], I was just unlucky. The first set here was frustrating and I was struggling - but I'm very happy with the second and third."

In the men's doubles, Britain's Henry Patten and Finnish team-mate Harri Heliovaara fell to defeat in their second match.

The world number ones and defending champions won the first set but were beaten 6-7 (5-7) 6-3 10-4 by fourth seeds Marcelo Arevalo and Mate Pavic.

articles.title: Zverev pasa a semifinales de las ATP Finals y evita la eliminación de Jódar
articles.standfirst: El número 1 supera a Shelton en dos sets y suma siete victorias con el americano en la misma cifra de partidos
articles.summary: El flamante número 1 mundial supera al americano en dos sets
articles.body: un día después de recibir el trofeo que le acredita como número 1 mundial a final de temporada, Alexander Zverev ha dado muestras de esa condición en el segundo partido del grupo John McEnroe contra Ben Shelton, con el liderato y el pase a las semifinales en juego. El alemán ha dado buena cuenta del estadounidense, por 6-2 y 7-6(4), y se convierte en el primer semifinalista de Turín. Ya son siete victorias en otros tantos partidos con el mismo rival. Zverev no superaba a un 'top5' mundial precisamente desde que hace un año acabó con la resistencia de Ben también en la fase de grupos. "Desconocía que el triunfo me daba el pase. Yo sé que si juego un buen tenis los resultados vendrán por si solos", reflexionaba a la conclusión. El jueves se jugará con Arthur Fils un botín de 200 puntos más y un talón de 405.000 dólares. La victoria de Sascha mantiene vivas las mínimas esperanzas de clasificación de Rafa Jódar. El madrileño necesita ahora ganar a Shelton en dos sets este jueves y esperar a que el tenista de Hamburgo haga lo mismo con Fils para que se produzca un triple empate.
